chapters: The vision of Yeshayahu the son of Amotz, which he saw concerning Yehudah and Yerushalayim, in the days of Uziyahu, Yotam, Achaz, and Chizkiyahu, kings of Yehudah.
Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for Havayah has spoken; Children I have raised and exalted, yet they have rebelled against Me.
An ox knows his owner and a donkey his master's crib; Yisroel does not know, my people does not consider.
Woe to a sinful nation, a people heavy with iniquity, evildoing seed, corrupt children. They forsook Havayah; they provoked the Holy One of Yisroel; they drew backwards.
Why are you beaten when you still continue to rebel? Every head is afflicted with illness and every heart with malaise.
From the sole of the foot until the head there is no soundness — wounds and contusions and lacerated sores; they have not sprinkled, neither have they been bandaged, nor was it softened with oil.
Your land is desolate; your cities burnt with fire. Your land — in your presence, strangers devour it; and it is desolate as that turned over to strangers.
And the daughter of Tziyon shall be left like a hut in a vineyard, like a lodge in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
"Had not Havayah of Hosts left us a remnant, we would soon be like Sedom; we would resemble Amorah."
Hear the word of Havayah, O rulers of Sedom; give ear to the law of our Elokim, O people of Amorah!
Of what use are your many sacrifices to Me? Havayah says. I am sated with the burnt-offerings of rams and the fat of fattened cattle; and the blood of bulls and sheep and hegoats I do not want.
When you come to appear before Me, who requested this of you, to trample My courts?
You shall no longer bring vain meal-offerings, it is smoke of abomination to Me; New Moons and Shabbosos, calling convocations, I cannot bear iniquity with assembly.
Your New Moons and your appointed seasons My soul hates, they are a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
And when you spread out your hands, I will hide My eyes from you, even when you pray at length, I do not hear; your hands are full of blood.
Wash, cleanse yourselves, remove the evil of your deeds from before My eyes, cease to do evil.
Learn to do good, seek justice, strengthen the robbed, perform justice for the orphan, plead the case of the widow.
Come now, let us debate, Havayah says. If your sins prove to be like crimson, they will become white as snow; if they prove to be as red as crimson dye, they shall become as wool.
If you be willing and obey, you shall eat the best of the land.
But if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured by the sword, for the mouth of Havayah spoke.
How has she become a harlot, a faithful city; full of justice, in which righteousness would lodge, but now murderers.
Your silver has become dross; your wine is diluted with water.
Your princes are rebellious and companions of thieves; everyone loves bribes and runs after payments; the orphan they do not judge, and the quarrel of the widow does not come to them.
"Therefore," the Master says, Havayah of Hosts, the Mighty One of Yisroel, "Oh, I will console Myself from My adversaries, and I will avenge Myself of My foes.
And I will return My hand upon you and purge away your dross as with lye, and remove all your tin.
And I will restore your judges as at first and your counsellors as in the beginning; afterwards you shall be called City of Righteousness, Faithful City.
Tziyon shall be redeemed through justice and her penitent through righteousness.
And destruction shall come over rebels and sinners together, and those who forsake Havayah shall perish.
For they shall be ashamed of the elms that you desired, and you shall be humiliated because of the gardens that you chose.
For you shall be like an elm whose leaves are wilting, and like a garden that has no water.
And their strength shall become as tow, and its perpetrator as a spark, and both of them shall burn together, with no one to extinguish the fire.
The word that Yeshayahu, son of Amotz, prophesied concerning Yehudah and Yerushalayim.

And it shall be at the end of the days, that the mountain of Havayah's house shall be firmly established at the top of the mountains, and it shall be raised above the hills, and all the nations shall stream to it.

And many peoples shall go, and they shall say, "Come, let us go up to Havayah's mount, to the house of the Elokim of Yackov, and let Him teach us of His ways, and we will go in His paths," for out of Tziyon shall the Torah come forth, and the word of Havayah from Yerushalayim.

And he shall judge between the nations and reprove many peoples, and they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift the sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore.
"O house of Yackov, come and let us go in the light of Havayah."
For You have forsaken Your people, the house of Yackov, for they are full of witchcraft from the East and soothsayers like the Pelishtim, and with children of gentiles they please themselves.
And his land became full of silver and gold, without end to his treasures; and his land became full of horses, without end to his chariots.
And his land is full of idols; to the work of his hands he prostrates himself, to that which his fingers made.
And man has become bowed down, and man has become humble, and You shall not forgive them.
Come into the rock and hide in the dust, because of fear of Havayah and because of the splendor of His pride.
The haughty eyes of man will be humbled, and the height of men shall be bowed down, and Havayah alone shall be exalted on that day.
For Havayah of Hosts has a day over everyone proud and high, and over everyone exalted, and he shall become humble.
And over all the cedars of the Levanon, high and exalted, and over all the oaks of the Bashan;
And over all the high mountains and over all the exalted hills;
And over every lofty tower and over every fortified wall;
And over all the ships of Tarshish and over all coveted floors.
And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of man shall be humbled, and Havayah alone shall be exalted on that day.
And the idols shall completely pass away.
And they shall come into the caves of the rocks and into the hollows of the earth, because of the fear of Havayah and because of the splendor of His pride, when He rises to break the earth.
On that day, man will cast away his silver idols and his gold idols, which they made for him, before which to prostrate himself to moles and to bats.
To come into the clefts of the rocks and the hollows of the cliffs, because of the fear of Havayah and because of the splendor of His pride, when He rises to break the earth.
Withdraw yourselves from man whose breath is in his nostrils, for in what merit is he to be esteemed?
For, behold, the Master, Havayah of Hosts removes from Yerushalayim and from Yehudah a support and a stay, every support of bread and every support of water;
Hero and warrior; judge and prophet and soothsayer and elder;
Captain of fifty and man of esteem, and counsellor and skillful craftsman, and one who understands secrets.
And I will appoint youths as their princes, and scorners shall rule over them.
And the people shall be oppressed, man against man, and man against his fellow; they shall behave haughtily, the youth against the elder and the base against the honorable.
When a man shall seize his brother of the house of his father, saying, "You have a garment, be an officer to us, and this obstacle shall be under your hand,"
He shall swear on that day, saying, "I will not be a ruler, while in my house there is neither bread nor clothing; do not make me an officer over the people."
For Yerushalayim has stumbled, and Yehudah has fallen, for their tongue and their deeds are against Havayah, to provoke the eyes of His glory.
The recognition of their faces testified against them, and their sin, like Sedom they told, they did not deny; woe is to their soul, for they have paid themselves with evil.
Praise the righteous man for he is good, for the fruit of their deeds they shall eat.
Woe to the wicked who does evil, for the recompense of his hands shall be done to him.
As for My people, their rulers are mockers, and women govern them; O My people! Your leaders lead you astray, and the way of your paths they have destroyed.
The Havayah stands to plead, and He stands to judge the peoples.
The Havayah will enter into judgment with the elders of His people and their officers. And you have ravaged the vineyard; the spoils of the poor are in your houses.
What do you mean that you crush My people and the faces of the poor you grind? Havayah Elokim of Hosts says.

And Havayah said: Because the daughters of Tziyon are so haughty; and they walk with neck stretched forth, and winking eyes; walking and raising themselves they walk; and with their feet they spout "venom."
And Havayah shall smite with zaraath the crown of the heads of the daughters of Tziyon, and Havayah shall pour out their "vessels."
On that day, Havayah shall remove the glory of the shoes and the embroidered headdresses and the hairnets.
The necklaces and the bracelets and the veils,
The tiaras and the foot chains and the hair ribbons and the clasps and the earrings.
The finger-rings and the nose-rings.
The tunics and the bedspreads and the tablecloths and the purses.
The mirrors and the sheets and the turbans and the clasps.

And it shall come to pass, that, in the place of perfume, will be decay, and in the place of a girdle, laceration, and in the place of the deed, a wound that causes baldness, and in the place of the organ of levity, a sack-cloth girdle, for this is instead of beauty.
Your men shall fall by the sword and your heroism in war.
And her gates shall lament and mourn, and she shall be emptied out; she shall sit on the ground.
Now seven women shall take hold of one man on that day, saying, "Our bread we will eat, and our clothing we will wear. Only let your name be called on us; take away our reproach."
On that day, the sprout of Havayah shall be for beauty and for honor, and the fruit of the land for greatness and for glory for the survivors of Yisroel.
And it shall come to pass that every survivor shall be in Tziyon, and everyone who is left, in Yerushalayim; "holy" shall be said of him, everyone inscribed for life in Yerushalayim.
When Havayah shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Tziyon and the blood of Yerushalayim He shall rinse from its midst, with a spirit of judgment and with a spirit of purging.

And Havayah shall create over every dwelling of Mount Tziyon and over all those summoned therein, a cloud by day and smoke, and splendor of a flaming fire at night, for, in addition to every honor, there will be a shelter.
And a tabernacle shall be for shade by day from the heat, and for a shelter and for a covert from stream and from rain.
I will now sing for my beloved the song of my beloved about his vineyard; my beloved had a vineyard in a fertile corner.

And he fenced it in, and he cleared it of stones, and he planted it with the choicest vines, and he built a tower in its midst, and also a vat he hewed therein; and he hoped to produce grapes, but it produced wild berries.
And now, dwellers of Yerushalayim and men of Yehudah, judge now between me and between my vineyard.
What more could I have done for my vineyard that I did not do in it? Why did I hope to produce grapes and it produced wild berries?
And now, I will inform you what I am going to do to my vineyard. I will remove its hedge, and it shall be eaten up; breach its walls, and it shall be trampled.
And I will make it a desolation; it shall neither be pruned nor hoed, and the shamir and desolation will come up over it; and I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.

For the vineyard of Havayah of Hosts is the House of Yisroel, and the people of Yehudah are the plant of His joy; and He hoped for justice, and, behold, there was injustice; for righteousness, and behold, an outcry.
Woe to those who join a house to a house; a field to a field they draw near; until there is no place, and you will be settled alone in the midst of the land.
In my ears Havayah of Hosts spoke, "Truly, great houses shall become desolate, yea, large ones and good ones, without inhabitants.
For ten acres of vineyard will produce one bath, and the seed of a homer shall produce an ephah.
Woe to those who rise early in the morning; they pursue strong wine. They sit until late in the evening; wine inflames them.
And there are harp and lute, tambourine and flute, and wine at their drinking feasts; and the work of Havayah they do not regard, and the deed of His hands they have not seen.
Therefore, My people shall go into exile because of lack of knowledge, and its esteemed ones shall die of hunger, and its multitude shall be parched from thirst.
Therefore, the nether-world has expanded itself and opened its mouth without measure, and her splendor and her populace and multitudes, shall descend and those who rejoice therein.
And man shall be humbled, and man shall be brought low, and the eyes of the haughty shall be brought low.
And Havayah of Hosts will be exalted in judgment, and the Holy Elokim shall be hallowed with equity.
And lambs shall graze at their wont, and sojourners shall eat the ruins of the fat ones.
Woe to those who draw the iniquity with ropes of nothingness, and like cart ropes is the sin.
Those who say, "Let Him hurry; let Him hasten His deed, so that we may see; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Yisroel approach and come."
Woe to those who say of the evil that it is good and of the good that it is evil; who present darkness as light and light as darkness, who present bitter as sweet and sweet as bitter.
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and in their own estimation, of profound understanding.
Woe to the heroes to drink wine and valiant men to mix strong wine.
Those who exonerate the guilty one for reward of a bribe, and the innocence of the innocent they take away from him.

Therefore, as a flame of fire consumes stubble, and a flame shrivels straw, their root shall be like rot, and their blossom shall go up like dust, for they have rejected the law of Havayah of Hosts and the word of the Holy One of Yisroel they have despised.

Therefore, Havayah has become wroth with His people, and He has stretched forth His hand upon them and has struck them, and the mountains have quaked, and their corpses were like spittle in the midst of the streets; with all this, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still outstretched.
And He shall raise an ensign to the nations from afar, and He shall whistle to him from the end of the earth, and behold, quickly, swiftly he shall come.
None is weary or stumbles among them, he shall neither slumber nor sleep; the belt around his waist shall not open up, nor shall a thong of his shoes be torn.
One whose arrows are sharpened, and all his bows are bent, the hoofs of his horses are regarded like flint, and his wheels like the tempest.
He has a roar like a lion; he will roar like the lion cubs, and he will growl and lay hold of prey, and he will retrieve it, and no one will save it.
And he shall growl over it on that day like the growling of the sea, and he shall look to the land and behold darkness; the distressed one and the light shall darken in its eclipse.
In the year of the death of King Uziyahu, I saw Havayah sitting on a high and exalted throne, and His lower extremity filled the Temple.
Serafim stood above for Him, six wings, six wings to each one; with two he would cover his face, and with two he would cover his feet, and with two he would fly.
And one called out to the other and said, "Holy, holy, holy is Havayah of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory."
And the doorposts quaked from the voice of him who called, and the House became filled with smoke.
And I said, "Woe is me for I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips, and amidst a people of unclean lips I dwell, for the King, Havayah of Hosts have my eyes seen.
And one of the serafim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal; with tongs he had taken it from upon the altar.
And he caused it to touch my mouth, and he said, "Behold, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity shall be removed, and your sin shall be atoned for."
And I heard the voice of Havayah, saying, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?" And I said, "Here I am; send me."
And He said, "Go and say to this people, 'Indeed you hear, but you do not understand; indeed you see, but you do not know.'

This people's heart is becoming fat, and his ears are becoming heavy, and his eyes are becoming sealed, lest he see with his eyes, and hear with his ears, and his heart understand, and he repent and be healed."
And I said, "Until when, O Havayah?" And He said, "Until cities be desolate without inhabitant and houses without people, and the ground lies waste and desolate.
And Havayah removes the people far away, and the deserted places be many in the midst of the land.
And when there is yet a tenth of it, it will again be purged, like the terebinth and like the oak, which in the fall have but a trunk, the holy seed is its trunk."

And it came to pass in the days of Achaz son of Yotam son of Uziyahu, king of Yehudah, that Retzin, king of Aram, and Pekach son of Remalyahu, king of Yisroel, marched on Yerushalayim to wage war against it, and he could not wage war against it.
And it was told to the House of Dovid, saying, "Aram has allied itself with Efraim," and his heart and the heart of his people trembled as the trees of the forest tremble because of the wind.
And Havayah said to Yeshayahu, "Now go out toward Achaz, you and Shear-Yashuv your son, to the edge of the conduit of the upper pool, to the road of the washer's field.

And you shall say to him, "Feel secure and calm yourself, do not fear, and let your heart not be faint because of these two smoking stubs of firebrands, because of the raging anger of Retzin and Aram and the son of Remalyahu.
Since Aram planned harm to you, Efraim and the son of Remalyahu, saying:
'Let us go up against Yehudah and provoke it, and annex it to us; and let us crown a king in its midst, one who is good for us,'
So Havayah Elokim said, 'Neither shall it succeed, nor shall it come to pass.
For the head of Aram is Damesek, and the head of Damesek is Retzin; and in another sixty-five years, Efraim shall be broken, no longer to be a people.
And the head of Efraim is Shomron, and the head of Shomron is the son of Remalyahu; if you do not believe, it is because you cannot be believed."
And Havayah continued to speak to Achaz, saying,
"Ask for yourself a sign from Havayah, your Elokim: ask it either in the depths, or in the heights above."
And Achaz said, "I will not ask, and I will not test Havayah."
And he said, "Listen now, O House of Dovid, is it little for you to weary men, that you weary my Elokim as well?
Therefore, Havayah, of His own, shall give you a sign; behold, the young woman is with child, and she shall bear a son, and she shall call his name Imanu El.
Cream and honey he shall eat when he knows to reject bad and choose good.
For, when the lad does not yet know to reject bad and choose good, the land whose two kings you dread, shall be abandoned."
The Havayah shall bring upon you and upon your people and upon your father's house, days which have not come, since the day that Efraim turned away from Yehudah, namely, the king of Ashur.
And it shall be on that day, that Havayah shall whistle to the "fly" that is at the edge of the canals of Mitzrayim, and to the "bee" that is in the land of Ashur.
And they shall come and all of them shall rest in the desolate valleys and in the clefts of the rocks and in all the thornbushes and in all the shrines.
On that day, Havayah shall shave with the great razor on the other side of the river, on the king of Ashur, the head and the hair of the legs, and also the beard shall be entirely removed.
And it shall come to pass on that day, a man shall keep alive a heifer of the herd and two sheep.
And it shall be, because of the plentiful milk produced, that he shall eat cream, for everyone left in the land will eat cream and honey.
And it shall come to pass, that every place where there were a thousand vines for a thousand pieces of silver, will be for the worms and the thorns.
With arrows and with a bow shall one come there, for the whole land shall be worms and thorns.
And all the mountains that will be dug with a spade — the fear of worms and thorns shall not come there; it shall be for the pasture of oxen and for the treading of sheep.
And Havayah said to me, "Take for yourself a large scroll, and write on it in common script, to hasten loot, speed the spoils.
And I will call trustworthy witnesses to testify for Myself, Uriyah the priest and Zecharyah the son of Yeverechyahu."
And I was intimate with the prophetess, and she conceived, and she bore a son, and Havayah said to me, "Call his name Maher-Shalal-Chash-Baz.
For, when the lad does not yet know to call, 'Father' and 'mother,' the wealth of Damesek and the plunder of Shomron shall be carried off before the king of Ashur."
And Havayah continued to speak to me further, saying:
"Since this people has rejected the waters of the Shiloach that flow gently, and rejoice in Retzin and the son of Remalyahu,

Therefore, behold Havayah is bringing up on them the mighty and massive waters of the river — the king of Ashur and all his wealth, and it will overflow all its distributaries and go over all its banks.
And it will penetrate into Yehudah, overflowing as it passes through, up to the neck it will reach; and the tips of his wings will fill the breadth of your land, Imanu El.
Join together, O peoples, and be broken, hearken, all you of distant countries. Gird yourselves and be broken, gird yourselves and be broken.
Take counsel and it will be foiled; speak a word and it will not succeed, for Elokim is with us.
So has Havayah spoken to me with the overwhelming power of prophecy, and He admonished me from going in the way of this people, saying:
'You shall not call a band everything that this people calls a band; and you shall not fear what it fears nor attribute strength to it.
The Havayah of Hosts — Him shall you sanctify, and He is your fear, and He gives you strength.

And it shall be for a portent and a stone upon which to dash oneself and for a rock upon which to stumble for the two houses of Yisroel, who came to be for a snare and a trap for the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
And many shall stumble upon them, and fall and be broken, and be trapped and caught.
Bind this warning, seal the Torah in My disciples.'
And I will wait for Havayah, Who hides His countenance from the House of Yackov and I will hope for Him.
Behold, I and the children whom Havayah gave me for signs and for tokens in Yisroel, from Havayah of Hosts, Who dwells on Mount Tziyon.
And when they say to you, "Inquire of the necromancers and the Yid'onim, who chirp and who mutter." "Does not this people inquire of its Elokim? For the living, shall we inquire of the dead
For the Torah and for the warning?" If they will not say the likes of the thing, that it has no light.
And the one who passes therein shall suffer hardships and hunger, and it shall come to pass, when he is hungry and wroth, that he shall curse his king and his deity and face upwards.
And he shall look to the land, and behold, distress and darkness, weariness of oppression, and to the darkness he is lost.

For there is no weariness to the one who oppresses her; like the first time, he dealt mildly, exiling only the land of Zevulun and the land of Naftali, and the last one he dealt harshly, the way of the sea, and the other side of the Yarden, the attraction of the nations.
The people who walked in darkness, have seen a great light; those who dwell in the land of the shadow of death, light shone upon them.
You have aggrandized this nation; you have magnified the joy for them; they have rejoiced over You like the joy of harvest, as they rejoice when they divide spoils.
For, the yoke of his burden and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of the one who oppressed him have You broken, as on the day of Midyan.
For every victory shout sounds with clamor, and garments wallow in blood, but this shall be burnt, consumed by fire.

For a child has been born to us, a son given to us, and the authority is upon his shoulder, and the wondrous adviser, the mighty Elokim, the everlasting Father, called his name, "the prince of peace."

To him who increases the authority, and for peace without end, on Dovid's throne and on his kingdom, to establish it and to support it with justice and with righteousness; from now and to eternity, the zeal of Havayah of Hosts shall accomplish this.
The Havayah has sent a word against Yackov, and it has fallen in Yisroel.
And the entire people shall know — Efraim and the dwellers of Shomron — the fallacy of what they spoke with haughtiness and with arrogance, saying,
"Bricks have fallen, and hewn stones we will build; sycamores have been cut down, and we will replace them with cedars."
And Havayah strengthened the adversaries of Retzin over him, and his enemies He shall incite.
Aram from the east and the Pelishtim from the west, and they devoured Yisroel with every mouth; despite all this, His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still outstretched.
And the people has not returned to the One Who smites it, and Havayah of Hosts they have not sought.
And Havayah cut off from Yisroel a head and a tail, a large arch and a small arch in one day.
An elder and a man of esteem is the head, and a misleading prophet is the tail.
And the leaders of this people mislead, and those led by them are misled.

Therefore, over his youths, Havayah shall not rejoice, and on his orphans and his widows He shall not have mercy, for all of them are hypocrites and evil doers, and every mouth speaks obscene language; despite all this, His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still outstretched.
For wickedness has burnt like fire, and thorns shall consume them, and it kindled in the thickets of the forest, and they have become entangled by the thickening smoke.
By the wrath of Havayah of Hosts, the smoke has reached the earth, and the people has become like a conflagration of fire; no one has pity on his fellow-man.
And he snatched on the right and is still hungry, and he ate on the left and they are not sated; each one eats the flesh of his arm.
Menasheh with Efraim, and Efraim with Menasheh, together they shall unite against Yehudah; despite all this, His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still outstretched.
Woe to those who engrave engravings of injustice and missives of perverseness they write.
To pervert the judgment of the impoverished and to rob the judgment of the poor of My people, so that the widows are their plunder, and they pillage the orphans.
And what will you do for the day of visitation, and for the destruction that shall come from afar? To whom will you flee for aid, and where will you leave your riches?
Where he never knelt, in that place he will be a prisoner, and in that place they will fall slain; despite all this, His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still outstretched.
Woe that Ashur is the rod of My wrath, and My fury is a staff in their hands.
Against a hypocritical nation I will incite them, and upon the people of My anger will I command them, to plunder and to spoil spoils, and to make it trodden down like the mud of the streets.
But he does not deem it so, and his heart does not think so, but to destroy is in his heart, and to cut off nations, not a few.
For he says, "Are not my princes together kings?
Is not Kalno like Karkemish? Is it not like Arpad of Chamas? Will not Shomron be like Damesek?
As my hand was able to conquer the pagan kingdoms, and their graven images were from Yerushalayim and Shomron.
Indeed, as I did to Shomron and to her idols, so will I do to Yerushalayim and to her idols."

And it shall be, when Havayah completes all His work on Mount Tziyon and in Yerushalayim, I will visit retribution upon the increase of the arrogance of the king of Ashur's heart and upon the boasting of the haughtiness of his eyes.

For he said, "With the strength of my hand I accomplished it, and with my wisdom, for I am clever, and I remove the boundaries of peoples, and their positions have I plundered, and I lowered many inhabitants.
And my hand found the wealth of the peoples like a nest, and as one gathers abandoned eggs, I gathered the entire world, and no one moved a wing, or opened his mouth, or chirped."

Shall the axe boast over the one who hews with it, or shall the saw hold itself greater than he who wields it? It is as though the rod wields those who raise it. When the staff is raised, it is not the wood.
Therefore, the Master, Havayah of Hosts shall send leanness into his fat ones, and in the place of honor, a burning shall burn like the burning of fire.
And the light of Yisroel shall become fire, and his holy one shall become a flame, and it shall consume his thorns and his worms in one day.
And the glory of his forest and his stately forest, both soul and flesh shall it destroy, and it shall be as a tree eaten to powder by the worms.
And the remaining trees of his forest shall be few, and a lad shall write them.

And it shall come to pass that on that day the remnant of Yisroel and the survivors of the house of Yackov shall not continue to lean on him that smote them; but he shall lean on Havayah, the Holy One of Yisroel, in truth.
The remnant shall return, the remnant of Yackov, to the mighty Elokim.
For if your people Yisroel shall be like the sand of the sea, the remnant of them that shall return, shall wash away with righteousness the decreed destruction.
For destruction and annihilation Havayah Elokim of Hosts performs in the midst of all the land.
Therefore, so Havayah Elokim of Hosts said, "Fear not, my people who dwell in Tziyon, Ashur; with a rod may he smite you, and his staff may he bear over you in the way of Mitzrayim."
For in yet a very little while the fury shall be over, and My wrath, because of their blasphemy.
And Havayah of Hosts shall stir up a scourge against him, like the smiting of Midyan at the Rock of Orev, and His staff on the sea, and He shall carry him off after the manner of Mitzrayim.
And it shall come to pass on that day, that his burden shall be removed from upon your shoulder, and his yoke from upon your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of oil.
He came upon Ayas; he passed through Migron; at Michmas he deposits his luggage.
They crossed the ford; at Geva they lodged; Ramah quaked; Givat Shaul fled.
Raise your voice, Bat-Gallim; hearken, Layshah, Aniyah Anatot.
Madmenah wandered; the inhabitants of Geivim gathered.
Still today, he intends to stand in Nov; he waves his hand toward the mount of the daughter of Tziyon, the hill of Yerushalayim.
Behold the Master, Havayah of Hosts lops off the branches with a saw, and those of lofty height are hewn down, and the tall one shall be humbled.
And the thickets of the forests shall be cut off with iron, and the Levanon shall fall through a mighty one.
And a shoot shall spring forth from the stem of Yishai, and a twig shall sprout from his roots.
And the spirit of Havayah shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and heroism, a spirit of knowledge and fear of Havayah.
And he shall be animated by the fear of Havayah, and neither with the sight of his eyes shall he judge, nor with the hearing of his ears shall he chastise.

And he shall judge the poor justly, and he shall chastise with equity the humble of the earth, and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth and with the breath of his lips he shall put the wicked to death.
And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faith the girdle of his loins.
And a wolf shall live with a lamb, and a leopard shall lie with a kid; and a calf and a lion cub and a fatling shall lie together, and a small child shall lead them.
And a cow and a bear shall graze together, their children shall lie; and a lion, like cattle, shall eat straw.
And an infant shall play over the hole of an old snake and over the eyeball of an adder, a weaned child shall stretch forth his hand.
They shall neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mount, for the land shall be full of knowledge of Havayah as water covers the seabed.
And it shall come to pass on that day, that the root of Yishai, which stands as a banner for peoples, to him shall the nations inquire, and his peace shall be with honor.

And it shall come to pass that on that day, Havayah shall continue to apply His hand a second time to acquire the rest of His people, that will remain from Ashur and from Mitzrayim and from Patros and from Kush and from Eilam and from Shumer and from Chamas and from the islands of the sea.
And He shall raise a banner to the nations, and He shall gather the lost of Yisroel, and the scattered ones of Yehudah He shall gather from the four corners of the earth.
And the envy of Efraim shall cease, and the adversaries of Yehudah shall be cut off; Efraim shall not envy Yehudah, nor shall Yehudah vex Efraim.

And they shall fly of one accord against the Pelishtim in the west, together they shall plunder the children of the East; upon Edom and Moav shall they stretch forth their hand, and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

And Havayah shall dry up the tongue of the Mitzri Sea, and He shall lift His hand over the river with the strength of His wind, and He shall beat it into seven streams, and He shall lead the exiles with shoes.
And there shall be a highway for the remnant of His people who remain from Ashur, as there was for Yisroel on the day they went up from the land of Mitzrayim.
And you shall say on that day, "I will thank You, O Havayah, for You were wroth with me; may Your wrath turn away and may You comfort me.
Here is the Elokim of my salvation, I shall trust and not fear; for the strength and praise of the Eternal Havayah was my salvation."
And you shall draw water with joy from the fountains of the salvation.
And you shall say on that day, "Thank Havayah, call in His Name, publicize His deeds among the peoples; keep it in remembrance, for His Name is exalted.
Sing to Havayah for He has performed mighty deeds; this is known throughout the land.
Shout and praise, O dwellers of Tziyon, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Yisroel.
The harsh prophecy of Bavel which Yeshayahu son of Amotz prophesied.
On a tranquil mountain raise a banner, raise your voice to them; wave your hand that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
I commanded My prepared ones; I summoned My heroes to execute My wrath, those who rejoice in My pride.
The sound of a multitude in the mountains, the likeness of a numerous people, the sound of the stirring of kingdoms of nations gathering; Havayah of Hosts appoints officers over the warring host.
They come from a distant land, from the end of the heavens; Havayah and the weapons of His fury, to destroy all the land.
Lament, for the day of Havayah is near; like a raid from El Shaddai it shall come.
Therefore, all hands shall grow feeble, and the heart of every mortal shall melt.
And they shall panic; pangs and throes shall seize them; like a woman in confinement they shall writhe; each man shall be amazed at his fellow; their faces are faces of flames.
Behold, the day of Havayah is coming, cruel with wrath and burning anger, to make the land desolate, and its sinners He shall destroy from it.
For the stars of the heavens and its constellations shall not allow their light to illuminate, the sun has become dark in its going forth, and the moon shall not shine its light.
And I will visit evil upon the earth, and upon the wicked their iniquity; and I will cut off the pride of the presumptuous, and the arrogance of the tyrants I will humble.
I will make mortal man dearer than fine gold, and man dearer than the collection of the gold of Ofir.
Therefore, I will make heaven quake, and the earth will quake out of its place, because of the anger of Havayah of Hosts, and on the day of His burning wrath.
And he shall be like a roving deer, and like sheep who have no one to gather them; each man shall turn to his people, and each man shall flee to his land.
Everyone who is found shall be stabbed, and anyone who takes refuge shall fall by the sword.
And their babes shall be dashed before their eyes; their houses pillaged, and their wives ravished.
Behold I stir up Madai against them, who do not value silver, and do not desire gold.
And the bows shall dash youths, and on the newborn they shall not have mercy; on children their eye shall not look with pity.
And Bavel, the beauty of the kingdoms, the glory of the pride of the Kasdim, shall be like Elokim's overturning of Sedom and Amorah.
It shall not be settled forever, and it shall not be occupied from generation to generation, and no Aravi shall pitch his tent there, neither shall shepherds rest their flocks there.
And martens shall dwell there, and their houses shall be filled with ferrets, and ostriches shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there.
And cats shall dwell in his palaces, and serpents in the temples of pleasure, and her time is soon coming, and her days shall not be extended.
For Havayah shall have mercy on Yackov and again choose Yisroel, and He shall place them on their soil, and the strangers shall accompany them and join the House of Yackov.

And peoples shall take them and bring them to their place, and the House of Yisroel shall inherit them on the soil of Havayah, for slaves and maidservants, and they shall be captors to their captors and rule over those who dominate over them.
And it shall come to pass on the day Havayah allows you to rest from your sorrow and from your shuddering, and from the hard work that you were made to serve.
And you shall bear this parable against the king of Bavel, and you shall say, "How has the dominator ceased, has ceased the haughty one!
The Havayah has broken the staff of the wicked, the rod of the rulers.
Who would smite peoples with wrath, incessant blows, ruling nations with anger, pursued without relenting.
'All the land rested, became tranquil,' they opened their mouth in song.
Box trees, too, rejoiced at you, the cedars of the Levanon; 'Since you were laid low, the cutter will not come upon us.'
Gehinnom from beneath quaked for you, toward your arrival; it aroused for you the giants, all the chiefs of the earth; it caused all the kings of the nations to rise from their thrones.
All of them shall speak up and say to you, 'Have you too become weak like us? Have you become like us?'
Your pride has been lowered into Gehinnom, the stirring of your psalteries. Maggots are spread under you, and worms cover you.
How have you fallen from heaven, the morning star? You have been cut down to earth, You who cast lots on nations.
And you said to yourself, 'To the heavens will I ascend, above Elokim's stars will I raise my throne, and I will sit on the mount of the assembly, in the farthest end of the north.
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will liken myself to Elyon.'
But into the nether world shall you be brought down, to the bottom of the pit.
Those who see you shall look at you; shall gaze earnestly at you, 'Is this the man who caused the earth to quake, who wrought havoc among the kingdoms?
Who made the land like a desert, and his cities he demolished; for his prisoners he did not open the house.
All kings of nations, all of them, lay in honor, each in his house.
But you were cast from your grave like a discarded sapling, in the garb of the slain, of those pierced by the sword, who descend to the stones of the pit, like a trampled corpse.
You shall not join them in burial, for you have destroyed your land, you have slain your people; the seed of evil-doers shall not be named forever.
Prepare a slaughter for his sons because of the iniquity of their forefathers, lest they rise and inherit the land, and fill the surface of the earth with enemies."
"And I will rise against them," Havayah of Hosts says, "and I will cut off from Bavel a name and a remnant, a son and a grandson," Havayah says.
"And I will make it for a heritage of hedgehogs and pools of water, and I shall sweep it away with a broom of destruction," Havayah of Hosts says.
The Havayah of Hosts swore saying, if not as I thought, so it was, and as I planned, so it shall remain.
To break Ashur in My land, and on My mountains will I trample him, and his yoke shall be removed from upon them, and his burden shall be removed from upon his shoulder.
This is the plan that is planned over the entire land, and this is the outstretched hand over all the nations.
For Havayah of Hosts planned, and who will frustrate it? And it is His hand that is outstretched, and who will return it?
In the year of King Achaz' death, was this harsh prophecy.
Rejoice not, Peleshet, all of you, that the rod that smote you has been broken, for, from the root of a snake shall emanate a venomous serpent, and his offspring is a fiery flying serpent.
And the firstborn of the poor shall graze, and the paupers shall lie in safety, and I will put your root to death through hunger, and he shall slay your remnant.
Howl for the gate, cry out for the city; Peleshet has melted, all of you, for from the North smoke has come, and there is no straggler in his ranks.
Now what shall the messenger of a nation announce? That Havayah has founded Tziyon, and therein shall the poor of His people shelter themselves.

The harsh prophecy concerning Moav, for on the night that Ar of Moav was pillaged, it was as though they were sleeping silently, for on the night that Kir of Moav was pillaged, it was as though they were sleeping silently.
They went up to the temple, and Divon to the high places to weep; for Nevo and for Meidva shall Moav lament; on all their heads is baldness; every beard is shaven.
In its streets they girded themselves with sackcloth; on its roofs and in its city squares they all wail, sighing with weeping.
And Cheshbon and Elaleh cried out; as far as Yahatz, their voice was heard; therefore, the armed men of Moav shall cry in alarm; their soul shall cry for them.

My heart shall cry out for Moav; its bars as far as Tzoar as a third-born heifer; for the ascent of Haluchis, amidst weeping shall they ascend it, for in the way of Choronayim, a cry of destruction they shall raise.
For the waters of Nimrim shall be a waste, for the grass has dried out, herbage has vanished; vegetation is no more.
Because of the many things they did, and their appointed territory by the western sea, they shall take them.
For the cry has surrounded the border of Moav; as far as Eglayim is her wail and to Beer — elim is her wail.
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood, for I will place upon Dimon additions; for the survivors of Moav is the lion, and for the remnant is the land.
Send lambs of the ruler of the land from Sela Midbarah to the mountain of the community of Tziyon.
And it shall be like a wandering bird, driven from the nest; shall the villages of Moav be at the fords of Arnon.
Bring counsel, deliberate judgment, make like the night your shadow at noon; conceal the exiles, reveal not the wanderer.

May My exiles sojourn among you, Moav. Become a hiding place for them from before the plunderer, for the milking has come to an end; the udders have vanished; the tramplers have ceased from the earth.
And the throne shall be established through loving-kindness, and there shall sit thereon in truth in the tent of Dovid, one who judges and demands justice and performs righteousness.
We heard the pride of Moav, they have become very proud; their pride and their haughtiness and their conception are improper, as are their branches.
Therefore, Moav shall wail for Moav; they shall all wail; for the walls of Kir-Chareset shall you lament, but brokenhearted.

For the grain fields of Cheshbon have become desolate; the vine of Sivmah, the chiefs of nations have broken its saplings; they reached as far as Yazer; they strayed to the desert; its tendrils spread out, crossed the sea.
Therefore, I will weep with the weeping of Yazer, for the vine of Sivmah; I will be sated over you with my tears, Cheshbon and Elaleh, for over your figs and over your harvest a shout has fallen.
And joy and gladness shall be terminated from the fruitful field, and in the vineyards there shall be neither song nor shout; no treader shall tread wine into the pits; the shout have I abolished.
Therefore, my bowels shall moan for Moav like a harp, and my innards for Kir-Cheres.
And it shall come to pass, when it shall appear that Moav has wearied of waging war on the high place, and he shall enter his sanctuary to pray and he shall not be able.
This is the word that Havayah spoke concerning Moav long ago.
And now, Havayah has spoken saying, "In three years like the years of a hireling, the glory of Moav shall be debased, among all the great multitude, and the remnant shall be very few, not many."
The harsh prophecy concerning Damesek; Behold Damesek shall be removed from being a city, and it shall be a depth of ruins.
The cities of Aroer shall be abandoned; for the flocks shall they be, and they shall lie undisturbed.
And a fortress shall cease from Efraim and a kingdom from Damesek, and the remnant of Aram; like the glory of the children of Yisroel shall they be, Havayah of Hosts says.
And it shall come to pass on that day, that the glory of Yackov shall become impoverished and the fatness of his flesh shall become emaciated.
And it shall be like gathering the harvest of the standing grain, and his arm reaps ears, and he shall be as one who gathers ears of grain in the valley of Refaim.

And gleanings shall be left in it like the cutting of an olive tree, two or three berries at the end of the uppermost bough; four or five on its branches when it produces fruit, Havayah says, Elokim of Yisroel.
On that day, man shall turn to his Maker, and his eyes shall look to the Holy One of Yisroel.
And he shall not turn to the altar of the work of his hands, and what his fingers made he shall not regard, neither the asherim nor the sun-images.
On that day, the cities of his strength shall be like the abandonment of the forest and the many branched trees which they abandoned from before the children of Yisroel, and it became a waste.
For you forgot the Elokim of your salvation, and the Rock of your strength you did not remember; because I planted you with pleasant saplings, and with the branch of a stranger you sow it.
On the day of your planting you mingled, and in the morning you cause your seed to blossom; a heap of harvest on a day of sickness and mortal pain.
Woe to a multitude of many peoples, like the roaring of seas they roar; and a rushing of nations, like the rushing of mighty waters they rush.

Nations, like the rushing of many waters, they rush, and He shall rebuke them, and he shall flee from afar, and he shall be pursued like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the thistle blossoms before the tempest.
At eventide, behold there is fright; before morning he is no more. This is the portion of our plunderers and the lot of our spoilers.
Woe to the land shaded by wings, which is on the other side of the rivers of Kush.

Who sends emissaries in the sea and in boats of bulrushes on the surface of the water, "Go, swift messengers, to a nation, pulled and torn, to an awesome nation from their beginning onward, a nation punished in kind and trampled, whose land the rivers have plundered.
All inhabitants of the world and dwellers of the earth, when a standard of the mountains is raised you shall see, and when a shofar is sounded you shall hear.
For so has Havayah said to me, "I will rest, and I will look down upon My dwelling-place, like a clear heat upon herbs, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
For behold the harvest when the blossom is past, and the buds turn into ripening grapes, and he shall cut off the tendrils with pruning-hooks, and the roots he removed, he cut them off.
They shall be left together to the birds of the mountains and to the beasts of the earth, and the birds shall spend the summer upon them and the beasts of the earth shall spend the winter upon them.

At that time, there shall be brought a gift to Havayah of Hosts, a people pulled and torn, and from an awesome people from its beginning and onward, a nation punished in kind and trampled, whose land the rivers have plundered, to the place of the name of Havayah of Hosts, Mount Tziyon.

The harsh prophecy of Mitzrayim; Behold Havayah is riding on a light cloud and He shall come to Mitzrayim, and the idols of Mitzrayim shall quake from before Him and the heart of the Mitzrim shall melt in their midst.
And I will stir up Mitzrim against Mitzrim, and they shall war one man against his brother, and a man against his friend, a city against a city and a province against a province.

And the spirit of Mitzrayim shall empty out in its midst, and I will thwart its counsel, and they shall turn to the idols and to the sorcerers and to the necromancers and to those who divine by the jidoa bone.
And I will deliver the Mitzrim into the hands of a harsh master, and a mighty king shall rule over them; so the Master says, Havayah of Hosts.
And water from the sea shall dry up, and the river shall dry up and become arid.
And they shall abandon the rivers; the deep canals shall become impoverished and dried up; reeds and rushes shall be cut off.
The well-rooted plants by the stream, by the brink of the stream, and all that is planted by the stream shall dry up, be driven away, and be no more.
And the fisherman shall lament and mourn, all who cast fishhooks into the stream; and those who spread nets on the surface of the water shall be cut off.
And those who work at flax to be combed and those who weave nets shall be ashamed.
And its foundations shall be crushed, all who make dams for still ponds.
Indeed, the princes of Tzoan are fools, the wise advisors of Paroh have foolish counsel; how do you say to Paroh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of the kings of old."
Where then are your wise men who will tell you now, and who will know what Havayah of Hosts planned concerning Mitzrayim?
The princes of Tzoan have become foolish; the princes of Nof have been misled; they have misled Mitzrayim, the cornerstone of its tribes.
The Havayah has poured into its midst a spirit of perverseness, and they have misled Mitzrayim in all its deeds as a drunkard strays in his vomit.
And Mitzrayim shall not have any deed that either the head or the tail, the branch or the rush shall do.
On that day, Mitzrayim shall be like women, and it shall quake and dread the raising of the hand of Havayah of Hosts, which He shall raise over it.
And the land of Yehudah shall be to Mitzrayim for a dread; anyone who mentions it to him, he will dread, because of the plan of Havayah of Hosts, which He is planting against him.
On that day there shall be five cities in the land of Mitzrayim speaking the language of Kena'an and swearing to Havayah of Hosts, one of which will be called "the city of Cheres."
On that day there shall be an altar to Havayah in the midst of the land of Mitzrayim, and a monument beside its border, to Havayah.

And it shall be for a sign and for a witness to Havayah of Hosts in the land of Mitzrayim, for they shall cry out to Havayah because of oppressors, and He shall send them a savior and a prince, and he shall save them.

And Havayah shall be known to the Mitzrim, and the Mitzrim shall know Havayah on that day, and they shall serve with a sacrifice and a meal offering, and they shall make vows to Havayah and they shall fulfill them.
And Havayah shall plague Mitzrayim, plaguing and healing, and they shall return to Havayah, and He shall accept their prayer and heal them.
On that day there shall be a highway from Mitzrayim to Ashur, and Ashur shall come upon Mitzrayim, and Mitzrayim shall come upon Ashur, and Mitzrayim shall serve with Ashur.
On that day, Yisroel shall be a third to Mitzrayim and to Ashur; a blessing in the midst of the land.
Which Havayah of Hosts blessed them, saying, "Blessed is My people Mitzrayim, and the work of My hands Ashur, and My heritage Yisroel."
During the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Ashur sent him, and he waged war with Ashdod and captured it.

At that time, Havayah spoke through Yeshayahu son of Amotz, saying: "Go, and you shall gird a sackcloth over your loins and you shall remove your shoes from your feet." And he did so, going naked and barefoot.
And Havayah said, "As My servant Yeshayahu has gone naked and barefoot for three years, as a sign and a symbol for Mitzrayim and for Kush,
So shall the king of Ashur lead the captivity of Mitzrayim and the exile of Kush, youths and old men, naked and barefoot, with bare buttocks, the shame of Mitzrayim.
And they shall be broken and ashamed because of Kush, their expectation, and because of Mitzrayim, their boasting.
And the inhabitants of this isle shall say on that day, "Behold, so is our expectation where we fled for aid because of the king of Ashur, and how will we escape?
The harsh prophecy of the western desert; like tempests in an arid land, to pass, coming from the desert, from an awesome land.
A harsh prophecy was told to me; The traitor shall be betrayed and the plunderer shall be plundered; march, O Eilam, Besiege, O Madai! All sighs have I brought to an end.
Therefore, my loins are filled with trembling; pangs have seized me like the pangs of a woman in labor; I have become confused from hearing; I have become frightened from seeing.
My heart has strayed; fright has terrified me; the evening of my desire He has made for me into trembling.
Setting the table, setting up the lamp, eating, drinking; "Arise, princes, anoint a shield!"
For so has Havayah said to me, "Go, set up the lookout; what he sees he will tell.
And he shall see a chariot with a pair of riders; one riding a horse and one riding a camel, and he shall listen attentively.
And the lion called, "On the watchtower, O Havayah, I always stand by day, and on my watch I stand all the nights.
And behold this is coming, a chariot of men, a pair of riders." And he called out and said, "Bavel has fallen, yea, it has fallen, and all its graven idols he has dashed to the earth."
My threshed grain and the product of my threshing floor. What I heard from Havayah of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisroel, I have related to you.
The harsh prophecy of Dumah: To me one calls from Seir, "Watchman, what will be of the night? Watchman, what will be of the night?"
Said the watchman, "Morning has come, and also night. If you will request, request. Return and come."
The harsh prophecy concerning Arav: In the forest in Arav did you lodge, on the roads of your cousins.
Toward the thirsty they bring water; the inhabitants of the land of Teima with his bread they came before the wanderer.
For, because of the swords they wandered; because of the outstretched sword, because of the bent bow, and because of the pressure of war.
For so has Havayah said to me: "In another year, like the days of a hireling, all the glory of Keidar shall terminate.
And the rest of the number of the bows of the heroes of the children of Keidar shall decrease, for Havayah, the Elokim of Yisroel has spoken."
The harsh prophecy of the Valley of Vision: What ails you then that all of you have gone up to the rooftops?
Full of clamor, a tumultuous city, a happy city, your fallen have not fallen by the sword, nor have they died in war.
All your officers wandered together, because of the bow they were bound; all those found of you were bound together; from afar they fled.
Therefore, I said, "Leave Me alone; let Me cry bitterly; do not hasten to console Me concerning the pillaging of the daughter of My people."
For it is a day of breaking and trampling and confusion to Havayah Elokim of Hosts in the Valley of Vision, destroying the wall and shouting, "To the mountain!"
And Eilam carried a quiver with a chariot of men, riders, and to the wall they attached their shields.
And it came to pass that the choice of your valleys were filled with chariots and the riders laid siege to the gate.
And he bared the covert of Yehudah, and you looked on that day to the weapons of the house of the forest.
And the cracks of the city of Dovid you saw that they had increased, and you gathered the water of the lower pool.
And the houses of Yerushalayim you counted, and you demolished the houses to fortify the wall.
And a ditch you made between the two walls and the water of the old pool, but you did not look to its Maker, and Him Who fashioned it from afar, you did not see.
And Havayah Elokim of Hosts called on that day, for weeping, and for lamenting and for baldness, and for girding with sackcloth.
And behold, joy and happiness, slaying cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine; "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."
"And it was revealed in My ears, Havayah of Hosts; I, therefore, swear that this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die, Havayah Elokim of Hosts said.
So Havayah Elokim of Hosts said: Go, come to this voluptuary, to Shevna, who is appointed over the Temple.
What have you here, and whom have you here, that you have hewn for yourself here a grave? He hews his grave on high; he hews a habitation for himself in the rock.
Behold, Havayah shall cast you about with a mighty toss, and cause you to fly.

He shall wind you around like a turban, like a surrounding wall, to a land of ample space; there you shall die, and there shall the chariots of your glory become the shame of the house of your master.
And I will cast you off your position, and from your station He shall tear you down.
And it shall come to pass on that day, that I will call My servant, Elyakim son of Chilkiyah.

And I will dress him with your tunic, and with your girdle I will gird him, and your authority will I place into his hand, and he shall become a father to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim and to the house of Yehudah.
And I will give the key of the House of Dovid on his shoulder, and he shall open and no one shall close; and he shall close and no one shall open.
And I will thrust him like a peg in a sure place, and it shall become a throne of glory for his father's house.
And they shall hang upon him all the honor of his father's house, the children and the grandchildren, all the small vessels, from the vessels of basins to all the vessels of the lyres.
On that day, Havayah of Hosts says, shall the peg, thrust in a permanent place, move, and it shall be cut off and fall, and the burden which is upon it shall be cut off, for Havayah has spoken.
The harsh prophecy concerning Tzor: Wail, ye ships of Tarshish, for it has been pillaged from within, from coming; from the land of the Kittim he appeared to them.
Be silent, ye island dwellers; the merchants of Tzidon, the seafarers replenished you.
And on great waters, the seed of Shichor, the harvest of the Yeor was her revenue, and she became the mart of the nations.
Be ashamed, for the sea said, the stronghold of the sea, saying, "I have not travailed, nor have I borne, neither have I reared young men nor have I raised virgins."
Like the report concerning Mitzrayim, shall they quake at the report of Tzor.
Proceed to Tarshish, wail, ye island dwellers!
Is this your joyful city from ancient times, whose feet carry her afar to sojourn?
Who planned this on the royal Tzor, whose merchants were princes, whose traffickers were the honored of the earth?
The Havayah of Hosts planned it, to profane the pride of every position, to bring contempt upon all the honored of the earth.
Cross your land like a river, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no more strength.
He stretched His hand over the sea; He aroused kingdoms; Havayah commanded upon Kena'an, to destroy its strongholds.
And He said, "You shall no longer continue to rejoice, O plundered one, O virgin daughter of Tzidon; arise, cross over to Kittim; even there you shall have no rest.
Behold the land of the Kasdim, this people has never been; Ashur established it for fleets; they erected its towers, destroyed its palaces, made it for a ruin.
Wail, O ships of Tarshish for your stronghold has been spoiled.
And it shall come to pass on that day, that Tzor shall be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king; at the end of seventy years, it shall fare with Tzor like the song of the harlot.
Take a harp, go around the city, O forgotten harlot; play well, sing many songs, so that you shall be remembered.

And it shall be at the end of seventy years, that Havayah shall remember Tzor, and she shall return to her hire, and she shall have commerce with all the kingdoms of the earth upon the surface of the earth.

And her commerce and her hire shall be holy to Havayah, it shall not be stored nor shall it be inherited, but those who sit before Havayah shall have her commerce to eat their fill and for stately clothing.
Behold Havayah empties the land and lays it waste, and He shall turn over its face and scatter its inhabitants.

And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest, as with the slave, so with his master, as with the maidservant, so with her mistress, as with the buyer, so with the seller, as with the lender, so with the borrower, as with the creditor, so with the one who owes him.
The land shall be emptied and it shall be pillaged, for Havayah has spoken this thing.
The land has mourned, it has withered, the land has been humbled and withered, the highest of the people of the land have been humbled.
And the land has deceived because of its inhabitants, for they transgressed instructions, infracted statutes, broke the everlasting covenant.
Therefore, an oath has consumed the land, and the inhabitants thereof were wasted; therefore, the inhabitants of the land were dried up, and few people remained.
Wine mourns, the vine is humbled, all joyful hearted sigh.
The joy of the drums has stopped, the stirring of merrymakers has ceased, the joy of the harp has stopped.
In song they shall not drink wine; strong drink shall become bitter to those who drink it.
The wasted city is broken; every house is closed from entering.
A cry for wine is in the streets; all joy is darkened; the joy of the land is exiled.
In the city there remains ruin; through desolation the gate is battered.
For so shall it be in the midst of the land among the peoples, like the cutting of the olive tree, like the gleanings when the vintage is over.
They shall raise their voice, they shall sing; of the pride of Havayah they shall shout for joy more than by the sea.
Therefore, for the lights honor Havayah; in the islands of the sea, the Name of Havayah Elokim of Yisroel.

From the end of the earth we heard songs, "The righteous shall be upraised." And I said, "I have my secret; woe is to me! the treacherous have dealt treacherously; yea, the treacherous have dealt very treacherously."
Fright and a pit and a trap shall come upon you, inhabitant of the land.

And it shall come to pass, that he who flees from the sound of the fright shall fall into the pit, and he who ascends from within the pit shall be snared in the trap, for windows from above have been opened and the foundations of the earth have trembled.
The earth has broken; the earth has crumbled; the earth totters.
The earth sways like a drunken man, and it sways like a lodge, and its transgression shall weigh down upon it, and it shall fall and not continue to rise.
And it shall come to pass on that day, that Havayah shall visit punishment upon the host of heaven on high and upon the kings of the earth on the earth.
And they shall be gathered a gathering as prisoners into a dungeon, and they shall be shut up in the prison, and sins of many days shall be visited upon them.
And the moon shall be ashamed and the sun shall be abashed, for Havayah of Hosts has reigned in Mount Tziyon and in Yerushalayim, and before His elders will be glory.
You are Havayah, my Elokim: I will exalt You, I will praise Your name, for You have dealt wondrously; counsels from long ago in true faith.
For You made from a city a heap, a fortified city into a ruin; a palace of strangers, because of the city, it shall never be rebuilt.
Therefore, shall a strong people honor You; a city of tyrannical nations shall fear You.
For You were a fortress for the poor, a fortress for the pauper in time of his distress, a shelter from pouring rain, a shade from heat, for the spirit of the tyrants is like a flood against a wall.
Like heat in the dry season, a multitude of strangers You shall humble; like heat with a thick cloud, so shall the downfall of the tyrants be sung.
And Havayah of Hosts shall make for all the peoples on this mount, a feast of fat things, a feast of dregs; fat things full of marrow, dregs well refined.
And He shall destroy on this mountain the face of the covering that covers all the peoples and the kingdom that rules over all the nations.
He has concealed death forever, and Havayah Elokim shall wipe the tears off every face, and the shame of His people He shall remove from upon the entire earth, for Havayah has spoken.
And they shall say on that day, "Behold, this is our Elokim: we hoped for Him that He would save us; this is Havayah for Whom we hoped; let us rejoice and be happy with His salvation.
For the hand of Havayah shall rest on this mount, and Moav shall be trampled in its place as the straw is trampled in the mire.
And he shall spread out his hands in his midst as the swimmer spreads out his hands to swim and He shall humble his haughtiness together with the cunning of His hands.
And the fortress of the strength of your walls He humbled. He brought it low; it reached the earth down to the dust.
On that day, this song shall be sung in the land of Yehudah: "The city that was our strength — salvation shall He place for walls and a bulwark.
Open the gates, so that a righteous nation, awaiting the realization of Elokim's promise, may enter.
The creature that relied, You shall guard, that there be peace, peace, for they trusted in You.
Trust in Havayah forever, for in Kah Havayah, is the Rock of eternity.
For He humbled the inhabitants of the high places, the fortified city; He brings it low, he brings it low even to the earth, he makes it reach even to the dust.
A foot shall trample it, the feet of a poor man, the soles of the impoverished.
The way of the righteous that is straight — O Upright One, the path of the righteous, You shall weigh.
Even for the way of Your judgments, O Havayah, have we hoped for You; for Your Name and for Your remembrance was the desire of our soul.
With my soul I longed for you at night; even with my spirit within me I beseeched You, for when Your judgments come to the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn justification.
Shall the wicked be favored — who did not learn righteousness? In the land of uprightness he deals unjustly, and he does not see the pride of Havayah.
O Havayah, Your hand has been taken away that they not see; let them see and be ashamed. The envy of a people, even the fire that shall consume Your enemies.
O Havayah, You shall prepare peace for us, for also the recompense for all our deeds have You dealt to us.
O Havayah, our Elokim, masters other than You have possessed us. Only concerning You will we mention Your name.
The dead shall not live, slackers shall not rise; therefore, You visited upon them and You destroyed them; You have put an end to any memory of them.
You have added to the nation, O Havayah; You have added to the nation and have been honored; You have rejected all the ends of the earth.
O Havayah, in their straits they remembered You; they pour out prayer when Your chastening is upon them.
As a pregnant woman comes near to give birth, she shudders, she screams in her pangs, so were we because of You, O Havayah.
We conceived, we shuddered, as though we bore wind; we wreak no salvations in the land, neither do the inhabitants of the world fall.
May Your dead live, 'My corpses shall rise; awaken and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for a dew of lights is your dew, and to the earth You shall cast the slackers.
Go, My people, come into your chambers and close your door about you; hide for but a moment, until the wrath passes.
For behold Havayah comes forth from His place to visit the iniquity of the dweller of the land upon him: and the land shall reveal its blood and it shall no longer conceal its slain ones.
On that day, Havayah shall visit with His hard and great and strong sword on leviathan the barlike serpent, and upon leviathan the crooked serpent, and He shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.
On that day, "A vineyard producing wine," sing to it.
I, Havayah, guard it, every moment I water it; lest He visit upon it, night and day I guard it.
I have no wrath; would that I were thorns and brier against the objects of My war! I would tread upon it and ignite it together.
If they would grasp My fortress, they would make peace for Me, they would make peace for Me.
Those who came, whom Yackov caused to take root, Yisroel flourished and blossomed and they filled the face of the world with fruitage.
Like the smiting who smote him did He smite him: like the slaying of his slain ones, was he slain?
In that measure, when they sent them out, it strove with it; He spoke with His harsh wind on the day of the east wind.

Therefore, with this shall Yackov's iniquity be atoned for, and this is all the fruit of removing his sin; by making all the altar stones like crushed chalkstones; asherim and sun-images shall not rise.
For a fortified city is solitary, a dwelling is forsaken and abandoned like a pasture; there a calf shall graze, and there he shall lie and consume its branches.

When its branches dry out, they shall be broken; women shall come and ignite it, for it is not a people of understanding; therefore, its Maker shall not have compassion on it, and He Who formed it shall not grant it favor.
And it shall come to pass on that day, that Havayah shall gather from the flood of the river to the stream of Mitzrayim, and you shall be gathered one by one, O children of Yisroel.

And it shall come to pass on that day, that a great shofar shall be sounded, and those lost in the land of Ashur and those exiled in the land of Mitzrayim shall come and they shall prostrate themselves before Havayah on the holy mount in Yerushalayim.
Woe is to the crown of the pride of the drunkards of Efraim and the young fruit of an inferior fig is the position of his glory, which is at the end of a valley of fatness, crushed by wine.
Behold Elokim has a strong and powerful wind, like a downpour of hail, a storm of destruction, like a stream of powerful, flooding water, He lays it on the land with His hand.
With the feet, they shall be trampled, the crown of the pride of the drunkards of Efraim.

And his glorious beauty shall be the young fruit of an inferior fig, which is on the head of the valley of fatness; as a fig that ripens before the summer, which, if the seer sees it, he will swallow it while it is still in his hand.
On that day, Havayah of Hosts shall be for a crown of beauty and for a diadem of glory, for the rest of His people.
And for a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and for might for those who bring back the war to the gate.

These, too, erred because of wine and strayed because of strong wine; priest and prophet erred because of strong wine, they became corrupt because of wine; they went astray because of strong wine, they erred against the seer, they caused justice to stumble.
For all tables were filled with vomit and ordure, without place.
Whom shall he teach knowledge and to whom shall he explain the message? To those weaned from milk, removed from breasts?
For a precept for a precept, a precept for a precept, a line for a line, a line for a line, a little there, a little there.
For with distorted speech and in another language, does he speak to this people.
For he said to them, "This is the rest; give rest to the weary, and this is the tranquility," but they would not listen.

And the word of Havayah shall be for them a precept for a precept, a precept for a precept, a line for a line, a line for a line, a little there, a little there, in order that they go and stumble backwards and be broken, and be trapped and caught.
Therefore, listen to the word of Havayah, men of scorn, allegorists of this people who are in Yerushalayim.

For you said, "We have made a treaty with death, and with the grave we have set a limit; when an overflowing scourge passes, it shall not come upon us, for we have made lies our shelter and in falsehood have we hidden ourselves.
Therefore, so has Havayah Elokim said: "Behold, I have laid as a foundation a stone in Tziyon, a fortress stone, a costly cornerstone, a foundation well founded; the believer shall not hasten.
And I will make justice the line, and righteousness the plummet, and hail shall sweep away the shelter of lies, and water shall flood the hiding place.
And your treaty with death shall be nullified, and your limit with the grave shall not endure; when an overflowing scourge passes, you shall be trampled by it.
When it passes, it shall take you, for every morning it shall pass, by day and by night, and it shall be only terror to understand the message.
For the bed is too short for one to stretch, and the ruler — it shall be narrow when he enters.
For like the mountain of breaches shall Havayah arise, like the valley in Givon He shall be incensed; to perform His deed, strange is His deed, and to perform His work, strange is His work.
And now, do not scorn, lest your pains become strong, for a complete destruction have I heard from Havayah Elokim of Hosts upon the entire land.
Give ear and listen to my voice; hearken and listen to my saying.
Shall the plowman plow all day to sow? Shall he open and harrow his soil?
Is it not so? When he smooths its surface, he scatters the black cumin and casts the cumin, and he places the prominent wheat, and the barley for a sign, and the spelt on its border.
And He shall chasten him justly, he whose Elokim directs him.
For not with a grooved implement is black cumin threshed, neither does a wagon wheel turn around on cumin, but black cumin is beaten with a staff and cumin with a rod.
Bread grain is crushed but it is not threshed forever, and the wheel of his wagon shall break, and its separators, he does not crush it.
This too comes forth from Havayah of Hosts: He gave marvelous counsel, made great wisdom.
Woe, Ariel, Ariel, the city wherein Dovid encamped! Add year to year, the festivals shall terminate.
And I will oppress Ariel, and there shall be moaning and mourning, and it shall be to Me like Ariel.
And I will encamp in a circle upon you, and I will besiege you with a camp of siege, and I will erect upon you siege works.

And you shall be humble, from the earth shall you speak and from the dust shall your speech be lowered; your voice shall be like a necromancer from the earth, and from the dust shall your speech chirp.
And the multitude of foreigners shall be like fine dust, and the multitudes of tyrants like passing chaff, and it shall be a sudden happening.
From Havayah of Hosts she shall be visited with thunder, with earthquake, and a great noise, storm wind and tempest, and a flame of consuming fire.
And shall be like a dream, a vision of the night, the multitude of all the nations assembled upon Ariel, and all those stationed around her and those who trap her, and those who besiege her.

And it shall be, as the hungry man dreams, and behold, he eats, and he shall awaken, and his appetite is unsated, and as the thirsty man dreams, and behold he drinks, and he shall awaken and behold he is faint, and his soul yearns, so shall be the multitude of all the nations gathered on Mount Tziyon.
Stop and wonder; they became blind and they blinded. They were intoxicated but not from wine; they reeled but not from strong wine.
For Havayah has poured upon you a spirit of deep sleep, and He has closed your eyes; the prophets and your heads who stargaze, He has covered.
And the vision of everything has been to you like the words of a sealed book, which they give to one who can read, saying, "Now read this," and he shall say, "I cannot, for it is sealed."
And if the book is given to one who cannot read, saying, "Now read this," he shall say, "I cannot read."

And Havayah said: "Because this people has come near; with their mouth and with their lips they honor Me, but their heart they draw far away from Me, and their fear of Me has become a command of people, which has been taught.
Therefore, I will continue to perform obscurity to this people, obscurity upon obscurity, and the wisdom of his wise men shall be lost, and the understanding of his geniuses shall be hidden.
Woe to those who think deeply to hide counsel from Havayah, and their deeds are in the dark. And they said, "Who sees us and who knows us?"
Shall your perversion be regarded like the potter's clay? Shall the thing made say of him who made it, "He did not make me," and the impulse say to the One Who formed it, "He does not understand"?
Indeed, in a short time, the Levanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be regarded as a forest.
And on that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and out of the obscurity and out of darkness shall the eyes of the blind see.
And those who suffered shall increase their joy in Havayah, and the impoverished people shall rejoice in the Holy One of Yisroel.
For the tyrants have ended and the scornful have been destroyed, and all those eager to commit violence shall be cut off.
Those who cause man to sin by a word, and him who reproves in the gate they trap, and they mislead the righteous through fraud.
Therefore, so Havayah said to the House of Yackov, Who redeemed Avraham, "Now Yackov shall not be ashamed, and now his face shall not pale.
For, when he sees his children, the work of My hands, in his midst, who shall hallow My name, and they shall hallow the Holy One of Yackov, and the Elokim of Yisroel they shall revere.
And those of straying spirit shall know understanding, and grumblers shall learn instruction.
"Woe to rebellious children," Havayah says, "to take counsel but not from Me, and to appoint a ruler but not of My spirit, in order to add sin upon sin.
Those who go to descend to Mitzrayim, and they have not asked of My mouth, to strengthen themselves with the strength of Paroh and to take shelter in the shade of Mitzrayim.
And the strength of Paroh shall be to you for shame, and the shelter in the shade of Mitzrayim for disgrace.
For his princes were in Tzoan and his emissaries reached Chaneis.
They all disgraced themselves because of a people that will not avail them, neither for aid nor for avail, but for shame and also for disgrace.

The burden of the beasts of the southland, in a land of trouble and anguish, the awesome lion and the crushing lion among them, the viper and the flying serpent; they carry their wealth on the shoulders of young donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people that will not avail.
And the Mitzrim help in vain and to no purpose, therefore, I called this, "They are haughty, idlers."
Now, come write it on a tablet with them, and on a book engrave it, and it shall be for the last day, forever to eternity.
For a rebellious people are they, lying children, children who would not hearken to Havayah's instruction.
