Who said to the seers, "You shall not see," and to the prophets, "You shall not prophesy for us true things. Speak to us with smooth talk; prophesy mockery.
Turn away from the road, turn away from the path, cease from before us the Holy One of Yisroel."
Therefore, so the Holy One of Yisroel said, "Because you have despised this matter, and you have put your trust in oppression and a perverse one, and you have relied upon it.
Therefore, this iniquity shall be to you as a breach of a falling wall, revealed in a fortified wall, whose breach will come suddenly."
And He shall break it like the breaking of a potter's jug, crushed without pity, and in its crushing shall not be found a shard, to scoop fire from a hearth, or to scoop water from a cistern.
For so Havayah Elokim said, the Holy One of Yisroel; "With tranquility and restfulness shall you be saved, with quietude and trust shall be your might; but you did not want.
And you said, 'No, but on horses will we flee.' Therefore, you shall flee. 'And on swift steeds will we ride.' Therefore, your pursuers shall be swift.
One thousand, because of the shout of one, because of the shout of five, shall you flee, until you remain like a mast on a mountaintop and like a flagpole on a hill."
Therefore, Havayah shall wait to be gracious to you, and therefore, He shall withdraw to have mercy upon you, for Havayah is a Elokim of justice; fortunate are all who wait for Him.
For a nation shall dwell in Tziyon, in Yerushalayim; you shall not weep; He shall be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; when He hears you, He shall respond to you.
And Havayah shall give you scant bread and water of oppression, and your Teacher shall no longer be concealed from you, and your eyes shall see your Teacher.
And your ears shall hear from behind you, saying, "This is the way; go on it," whether you will go right or whether you will go left.
And you shall contaminate the plate of your silver graven images and the adornment of your golden molten image; scatter them afar like a menstruant; 'Go out,' say to it.

And He shall give the rain of your seed, with which you shall sow the soil, and bread of the grain of the soil, and it shall be plenteous and fat; your livestock shall graze, each one becoming on that day a fattened lamb.
And the oxen and the young donkeys who work the soil shall eat enriched provender, which was winnowed with the shovel and with the fan.
And there shall be on every high mountain and on every raised hill, canals, rivulets of water, on the day of the great slaying, when the great ones fall.

And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold as the light of the seven days, on the day Havayah shall bind the fracture of His people, and the stroke of their wound He shall heal.
Behold the Name of Havayah comes from long ago, His wrath is kindled, and the weight of the burden; His lips are filled with fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.
And His breath is like a flooding stream, up to the neck it shall divide; to wave the nations with a vain waving, and a misleading bit on the jaws of the peoples.
This song shall be to you as the night of the sanctification of the festival, and the joy of heart like one who goes with a flute to come upon the mountain of Havayah, to the Rock of Yisroel.
And Havayah shall make heard the glory of His voice, and the laying down of His arm shall He show, with furious anger and a flame of consuming fire, bursting and storming rain, and hailstones.
For from Havayah's voice Ashur shall be broken; with a rod he would smite.
And it shall be, every place where the established staff shall pass, upon which Havayah shall grant peace, it shall be with drums and with harps, and with wars of waving will He fight with them.

For Tofteh is set up from yesterday, that too has been prepared for the king, it deepened, it widened its pile, of fire and much wood; the breath of Havayah is like a stream of brimstone, burning therein.

Woe to those who go down to Mitzrayim for aid, and who rely on horses and trust in chariots which are many, and on riders who are very strong, and they did not rely on the Holy One of Yisroel and Havayah they did not seek.
He too is wise, and He brought evil, and His words He did not retract; and He rose up on the house of evildoers and upon the aid of workers of iniquity.

Now the Mitzrim are men and not Elokim, and their horses are flesh and not spirit, and Havayah shall turn His hand, and the helper shall stumble and the helped one shall fall, and together all of them shall perish.

For so has Havayah said to me, "As a lion or a young lion growls over his prey, although a band of shepherds gather against him, from their voice he is not dismayed and from their stirring he is not subdued, so shall Havayah of Hosts descend to gather an army on Mount Tziyon and on its hill.
Like flying birds, so shall Havayah of Hosts protect Yerushalayim, protecting and saving, passing over and rescuing."
Return to Him, against Whom you have thought deeply to turn away, O children of Yisroel.
For on that day, they shall despise, each man his silver idols and his golden idols, which your hands have made for you for a sin.
And Ashur shall fall by the sword of one not a man, and the sword of one who is not a man shall consume him, and he shall flee from before a sword, and his chosen ones shall melt.
And his rock shall pass from fear, and his princes shall be dismayed at the miracle, the word of Havayah, whose fire is in Tziyon and Whose stove is in Yerushalayim.
Behold for righteousness shall a king reign, and over princes who rule with justice.
And the man shall be as a hiding-place from the wind and a shelter from the rain, as rivulets of water in an arid land, as the shade of a huge rock in a weary land.
And the eyes of them that see shall not be sealed,
And the heart of the hasty shall understand to know, and the ears of them that hear shall attend, and the tongue of the stammerers shall hasten to speak clearly.
A vile person shall no longer be called generous, nor shall a deceitful person be said to be noble.

For a vile person speaks villainly, and his heart works iniquity, to practice flattery, and to speak lies about Havayah, to empty the soul of the hungry, and the drink of the thirsty he causes to fail.
As for the deceitful person, his instruments are evil; he plans wicked plots, to destroy the poor with false words, and when the needy speaks a plea.
But the generous person plans generous deeds, and he, because of generous deeds, shall stand.
Complacent women, rise, harken to my voice, confident daughters, bend your ears to my speech.
Year after year, shall you be troubled, you confident ones, for the vintage has failed; the ingathering shall not come.
Tremble, complacent ones, to be troubled, confident ones, to undress and to bare, and to gird on the loins.
They shall beat on the breasts, lamenting, for the desirable fields, for the fruitful vines.
On my people's soil thorns and briers shall come up, for on all the houses of joy, the joyful city.
For the palace has been forsaken, the multitude of the city has been abandoned, rampart and tower are amidst ruins forever, a joy for wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks.
Until a spirit be poured us from on high, and the desert shall become a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be regarded as a forest.
And justice shall dwell in the desert, and righteousness shall reside in the fruitful field.
And the deed of righteousness shall be peace, and the act of righteousness shall be tranquility and safety until eternity.
And My people shall dwell in a dwelling of peace, and in secure dwellings and in tranquil resting-places.
And He shall hail down the hailing of the forest, and into the low state shall the city be humbled.
Fortunate are you who sow by all waters, those who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey.

Woe to you who spoil and you are not spoiled, and who deal treacherously, and they did not deal treacherously with you. When you finish your spoiling, you shall be spoiled, when you finish dealing treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with you.
O Havayah, be gracious to us! We have hoped for You. Be their arm every morning, also our salvation in time of trouble.
From the sound of roaring peoples have wandered; from Your exaltation, nations have scattered.
And your booty shall be gathered like the gathering of the locusts, like the roaring of the cisterns does he roar therein.
The Havayah is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Tziyon with justice and righteousness.
And the faith of your times shall be the strength of salvations, wisdom and knowledge; fear of Havayah, that is his treasure.
Behold for their altar they have cried in the street; ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
Highways have become desolate, the wayfarer has stopped; he has abrogated the treaty, despised cities, considered no man.
The land mourns, it has been cut off; he disgraced the Levanon, it was cut off; the Sharon became like the plain, and Bashan and Karmel have become emptied.
"Now I will rise," Havayah says. "Now I will be raised; now I will be exalted.
You shall conceive chaff; you shall bear stubble. Your breath is fire; it shall consume you."
And the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime; severed thorns, with fire they shall be burnt.
Hearken, you far-off ones, what I did, and know, you near ones, My might.
Sinners in Tziyon were afraid; trembling seized the flatterers, 'Who will stand up for us against a consuming fire? Who will stand up for us against the everlasting fires?'

He who walks righteously, and speaks honestly, who contemns gain of oppression, who shakes his hands from taking hold of bribe, closes his ear from hearing of blood, and closes his eyes from seeing evil.
He shall dwell on high; rocky fortresses shall be his defense; his bread shall be given him, his water sure.
The King in His beauty shall your eyes behold; they shall see from a distant land.
Your heart shall meditate in fear; where is he who counts, where is he who weighs, where is he who counts the towers?
A people of a strange tongue you shall not see, a people of speech too obscure to comprehend, of stammering tongue, without meaning.
See Tziyon, the city of our gathering; your eyes shall see Yerushalayim, a tranquil dwelling, a tent that shall not fall, whose pegs shall never be moved, and all of whose ropes shall not be torn.
But there, Havayah is mighty for us; a place of broad rivers and streams, where a galley with oars shall not go, and a great ship shall not pass.
For Havayah is our judge; Havayah is our ruler; Havayah is our king; He shall save us.
Your ropes are loosed, not to strengthen their mast properly; they did not spread out a sail; then plunder and booty were divided by many; the lame takes the prey.
And the neighbor shall not say, "I am sick." The people dwelling therein is forgiven of sin.
Nations, come near to hear, and kingdoms, hearken. The earth and the fullness thereof, the world and all its offspring.
For Havayah has indignation against all the nations and wrath against all their host. He has destroyed them; He has given them to the slaughter.
And their slain ones shall be thrown, and their corpses — their stench shall rise, and mountains shall melt from their blood.
And all the host of heaven shall melt, and the heavens shall be rolled like a scroll, and all their host shall wither as a leaf withers from a vine, and as a withered fig from a fig tree.
For My sword has become sated in the heaven. Behold, it shall descend upon Edom, and upon the nation with whom I contend, for judgment.

The Havayah's sword has become full of blood, made fat with fatness, from the blood of lambs and goats, from the fat of the kidneys of rams, for Havayah has a slaughter in Batzrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
And wild oxen shall go down with them, and bulls with fat bulls, and their land shall be sated from blood, and their dust shall become saturated from fat.
For it is a day of vengeance for Havayah, a year of retribution for the plea of Tziyon.
And its streams shall turn into pitch and its dust into sulfur, and its land shall become burning pitch.
By night and by day, it shall not be extinguished; its smoke shall ascend forever and ever; from generation to generation it shall be waste, to eternity, no one passing through it.
Pelican and owl shall inherit it, and night owl and raven shall dwell therein, and He shall stretch over it a line of waste, and weights of destruction.
As for its nobles, there are none who proclaim the kingdom, and all its princes shall be nothing.
And its palaces shall grow thorns, thistles and briers in its fortresses, and it shall be the habitat of jackals, an abode for ostriches.
And martens shall meet cats, and a satyr shall call his friend, but there the lilith rests and has found for herself a resting place.
There the owl has made its nest, and she has laid eggs and hatched them, and gathered its young under its shadow, but there have the vultures gathered, each one to her friend.
Seek out of the Book of Havayah and read; not one of them is missing, one did not miss her friend, for My mouth it has commanded, and its breath it has gathered them.
And He cast lots for them, and His hand distributed it to them with a line; forever they shall inherit it, to every generation they shall inhabit it.
Desert and wasteland shall rejoice over them, and the plain shall rejoice and shall blossom like a rose.

It shall blossom and rejoice, even to rejoice and to sing; the glory of the Levanon has been given to her, the beauty of the Karmel and the Sharon; they shall see the glory of Havayah, the beauty of our Elokim.
Strengthen weak hands, and make firm tottering knees.
Say to the hasty of heart, "Be strong, do not fear; behold our Elokim, with vengeance He shall come, the recompense of Elokim, that shall come and save you.
Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
Then the lame shall skip like a hart, and the tongue of the mute shall sing, for water has broken out in the desert and streams in the plain.
And the dry place shall become a pool, and the thirsty place shall become springs of water; in the habitat of jackals, a resting place, a grassy place for reeds and rushes.
And there shall be a highway and a road, and it shall be called the holy way; no unclean one shall traverse it, and it shall be for them; the traveler, even fools shall not go astray therein.
No lion shall be there, nor shall a profligate beast ascend thereon, it shall not be found there; and the redeemed ones shall go.

And the redeemed of Tziyon shall return, and they shall come to Tziyon with song, with joy of days of yore shall be upon their heads; they shall achieve gladness and joy, and sadness and sighing shall flee.
And it came to pass in the fourteenth year of King Chizkiyahu, that Sancheriv the king of Ashur came up against all the fortified cities of Yehudah and seized them.

And the king of Ashur sent Ravshakeh from Lachish to Yerushalayim to King Chizkiyahu with an army of a great multitude, and he stood near the conduit of the upper pool, on the road of the washer's field.
And Elyakim the son of Chilkiyah, who was appointed over the Temple and Shevna the scribe and Yoach the son of Asaf, the recorder, came out to him.
And Ravshakeh said to them, "Say now to Chizkiyahu, 'So has the great king, the king of Ashur, said, 'What is this confidence that you have trusted?'
I said, 'It is but words of the lips; counsel and might are needed for war. Now, on whom do you depend that you have rebelled against me?

Behold you have depended upon the support of this splintered reed, upon Mitzrayim, upon which a man will lean, and it will go into his palm and puncture it; so is Paroh the king of Mitzrayim to all who trust in him.

And if you say to me, 'We trust Havayah our Elokim,' is He not the one Whose high places and altars Chizkiyahu has removed? He has said to Yehudah and to Yerushalayim, 'Before this altar shall you prostrate yourselves.'
And now, wager now with my master the king of Ashur, and I will give you two thousand horses if you are able to supply riders upon them of your men.
And how can you repulse a captain, one of the smallest of my master's servants, and you rely on Mitzrayim for chariots and horsemen?
And now, is it with other than Havayah that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The Havayah said to me, 'Go up to this land and destroy it.' "

And Elyakim and Shevna and Yoach said to Ravshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramis for we understand it; do not speak with us in Yehudi within the hearing of the people who are on the wall."
And Ravshakeh said, "Did my master send me to speak these words to your master and to you? Is it not to the men who sit on the wall to eat their dung and drink their urine with you?"
And Ravshakeh stood and called in a loud voice in Yehudi, and he said, "Listen to the words of the great king, the king of Ashur!
So has the king said, 'Let not Chizkiyahu deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you.
And let not Chizkiyahu make you rely on Havayah, saying, 'The Havayah will save us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Ashur.'

Do not listen to Chizkiyahu, for so has the king of Ashur said, 'Make peace with me, and come out to me, and each man will eat of his vine and each man of his fig tree, and each man will drink the water of his cistern.
Until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards.'
Lest Chizkiyahu mislead you, saying, 'The Havayah will save us.' Have the gods of the nations saved each one his land from the hand of the king of Ashur?
Where are the gods of Chamas and Arpad, where are the gods of Sepharvayim? Now did they save Shomron from my hand?
Who are they among all the gods of the lands who saved their land from my hand, that Havayah should save Yerushalayim from my hand?"
And they remained silent and did not answer him even one word, for it was the king's order, saying, "Do not answer him."

And Elyakim the son of Chilkiyah who was appointed over the Temple and Shevna the scribe and Yoach the son of Asaf the recorder, came to Chizkiyahu, with torn garments, and they related to him the words of Ravshakeh.
And it was when King Chizkiyahu heard, that he rent his garments, and covered himself with sackcloth, and came to the house of Havayah.
And he sent Elyakim who was appointed over the Temple, and Shevna the scribe and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Yeshayahu the son of Amotz, the prophet.
And they said to him, "So has Chizkiyahu said, 'This day is a day of distress, proof and blasphemy, for the children have come as far as the birthstool and there is not strength to give birth.

Perhaps Havayah your Elokim will take note of the words of Ravshakeh whom the king of Ashur, his master, sent to blaspheme the living Elokim, and he brought proof with the words that Havayah your Elokim heard, and you shall offer up a prayer for the remnant that is found.' "
And King Chizkiyahu's servants came to Yeshayahu.
And Yeshayahu said to them, "So shall you say to your master, 'So has Havayah said, "Have no fear of the words you have heard, that the servants of the king of Ashur have blasphemed Me.
Behold I will imbue him with a desire, and he will hear a rumor and return to his land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his land." ' "
And Ravshakeh returned and found the king of Ashur waging war against Libnah, for he heard that he had left Lachish.
And he heard about Tirhakah the king of Kush, saying, "He has gone out to wage war against you." And he heard, and he sent emissaries to Chizkiyahu, saying,
"So shall you say to Chizkiyahu the king of Yehudah, saying, 'Let your Elokim, in Whom you trust, not delude you, saying, 'Yerushalayim shall not be given into the hands of the king of Ashur.'
Behold you have heard what the kings of Ashur have done to all the lands to destroy them. Now will you be saved?
Did the gods of the nations whom my forefathers destroyed — Gozan and Charan and Retzef and the children of Eden which is in Telassar — save them?
Where are the king of Chamas and the king of Arpad and the king of the city of Sepharvayim? He exiled them and he twisted them!' "
And Chizkiyahu took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read it; he went up to the house of Havayah, and Chizkiyahu spread it out before Havayah.
And Chizkiyahu prayed before Havayah, saying,
"O Havayah of Hosts, Elokim of Yisroel, Who dwells between the keruvim, You alone are the Elokim of all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
O Havayah, incline Your ear and listen, O Havayah, open Your eyes and see, and listen to all the words of Sancheriv, who sent to blaspheme the living Elokim.
Indeed, O Havayah, the kings of Ashur have destroyed all the countries and their land.
And committing their gods to fire, for they are not gods, but the handiwork of man, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
And now, O Havayah our Elokim, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You are Havayah alone."
And Yeshayahu the son of Amotz sent to Chizkiyahu, saying, "So has Havayah Elokim of Yisroel said, 'What you prayed to Me concerning Sancheriv, king of Ashur
This is the word that Havayah has spoken about him: 'The virgin daughter of Tziyon has despised you and has mocked you. The daughter has shaken her head at you.
Whom have you reviled and blasphemed, and upon whom have you raised your voice? And you have lifted your eyes on high against the Holy One of Yisroel.

Through your servants you have reviled Havayah, and you said, "With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of mountains, to the end of the Levanon, and I will cut down its tallest cedars, its choice cypresses, and I will come to its remotest height, to its farmland forest.
I dug and drank water, and I dry up with the soles of my feet all rivers of the siege."
Have you not heard from long ago what I did in days of yore, and what I formed? Now I have brought it, and it shall be to make desolate, blossoming hills, of fortified cities.
And their inhabitants became short of strength, broken and ashamed; they were like the grass of the field and green herbage, like grass of the roofs, and stubble before becoming standing grain.
And your sitting and your going out and your coming I know, and your raging against Me.
Because you have raged against Me, and your tumult has ascended into My ears, I will place My ring in your nose and My bit in your lips, and I will return you by the road by which you have come.

And this shall be the sign for you, this year you shall eat what grows by itself, and the next year what grows from the tree stumps, and in the third year, sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And the remaining survivors of the house of Yehudah shall continue to take root below and they shall produce fruit above.
For from Yerushalayim shall come forth a remnant, and survivors from Mount. Tziyon; the zeal of Havayah of Hosts shall do this.'

Therefore, so has Havayah said concerning the king of Ashur; 'He shall not enter this city, neither shall he shoot there an arrow, nor shall he advance upon it with a shield, nor shall he pile up a siege mound against it.
By the way he comes he shall return, and this city he shall not enter,' Havayah says.
'And I will protect this city to save it, for My sake and for the sake of My servant Dovid.' ' "
And an angel of Havayah went forth and slew one hundred eighty-five thousand of the camp of Ashur. And they arose in the morning, and behold they were all dead corpses.
And Sancheriv, the king of Ashur, left and went away, and he returned and dwelt in Ninveh.

And he was prostrating himself in the temple of Nisroch his deity, and Adram-Melech and Sharetzer, his sons, slew him by the sword, and they fled to the land of Ararat, and his son Esar-Chadon reigned in his stead.

In those days Chizkiyahu became critically ill, when Yeshayahu the son of Amotz, the prophet, came to him and said to him, "So has Havayah said, 'Give orders to your household, for you are going to die and you shall not live.
"And Chizkiyahu turned his face to the wall, and he prayed to Havayah.
And he said, "Please, O Havayah, remember now, how I walked before You truly and wholeheartedly, and I did what is good in Your eyes." And Chizkiyahu wept profusely.
And the word of Havayah came to Yeshayahu, saying,
"Go and say to Chizkiyahu, 'So has Havayah Elokim of your father Dovid said, "I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold I will add fifteen years to your life.
And from the hand of the king of Ashur will I save you and this city, and I will protect this city."
And this is your sign from Havayah, that Havayah will fulfill this word that He spoke.
Behold I return the shade of the steps that it went down on the steps of Achaz by the sun backwards ten steps, and the sun returned ten steps on the steps that it had descended.
The writing of Chizkiyahu, king of Yehudah, when he became ill and recovered from his illness.
I said, "In the desolation of my days will I go into the gates of the grave; I am deprived of the rest of my years."
I said, "I will not see the Eternal; the Eternal is in the land of the living; I will no longer look upon man, but I will be with those who dwell in withdrawal.
My generation was removed and exiled from me like a shepherd's tent; I severed, like a weaver, my life; from glory He shall deprive me; from day and night You shall finish me.
I made myself until morning like a lion, so it would break my bones; from day and night You shall finish me.
Like a crane and a swallow, so I chatter; I moaned like a dove. My eyes were lifted on high. O Havayah! Rob me! Pledge Yourself to me!
What shall I speak? He said to me, and He fulfilled it. I will cause all my sleep to flee because of the bitterness of my soul.
O Havayah! Concerning them, You said they shall live, and before all of them the life of my spirit, and You cured me and gave me life.
Behold for peace, it is bitter for me, yea it is bitter, and You desired my soul from the grave of decay, for You have cast behind You all my sins.
For the grave shall not thank You, nor shall death praise You; those who descend into the pit shall not hope for Your truth.
The living, the living, he shall thank You, like me today; a father shall inform his children of Your truth.
The Havayah has promised to save me, and we will play my hymns all the days of our life in the house of Havayah."
And Yeshayahu said, "Let them take a cake of pressed figs and lay it for a plaster on the boil, and it will heal."
And Chizkiyahu said, "What a sign that I will go up to the house of Havayah!"
At that time, Merodach-Baladan the son of Baladan, the king of Bavel, sent letters and a gift to Chizkiyahu when he heard that he had been ill and had recovered.

And Chizkiyahu rejoiced over them, and he showed them his entire treasure-house, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the good oil, and the entire house in which he kept his vessels, and everything that was found in his treasures; there was nothing that Chizkiyahu did not show them in his palace and in his kingdom.

And Yeshayahu the prophet came to King Chizkiyahu and said to him, "What did these men say, and whence did they come to you? " And Chizkiyahu said, "They have come to me from a distant country — from Bavel."
And he said, "What did they see in your palace?" And Chizkiyahu said, "They saw everything that is in my palace. There was nothing that I did not show them in my treasuries. "
And Yeshayahu said to Chizkiyahu, "Hearken to the word of Havayah of Hosts,
'Behold a time shall come when everything in your palace and what your forefathers have stored up, shall be carried off to Bavel; nothing shall remain,' Havayah said.
And they shall take some of your sons, who shall issue from you, whom you shall beget, and they shall be officers in the palace of the king of Bavel."
And Chizkiyahu said to Yeshayahu, "The word of Havayah that you have spoken is good." For he thought, "For there shall be peace and truth in my days."
"Console, console My people," says your Elokim.
Speak to the heart of Yerushalayim and call out to her, for she has become full from her host, for her iniquity has been appeased, for she has taken from the hand of Havayah double for all her sins.
A voice calls, "In the desert, clear the way of Havayah, straighten out in the wilderness, a highway for our Elokim."
Every valley shall be raised, and every mountain and hill shall be lowered, and the crooked terrain shall become a plain and the close mountains a champaign.
And the glory of Havayah shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see that the mouth of Havayah spoke.
A voice says, "Call!" and it says, "What shall I call?" "All flesh is grass, and all its kindness is like the blossom of the field.
The grass shall dry out, the blossom shall wilt, for a wind from Havayah has blown upon it; behold the people is grass.
The grass shall dry out, the blossom shall wilt, but the word of our Elokim shall last forever.
Upon a lofty mountain ascend, O herald of Tziyon, raise your voice with strength, O herald of Yerushalayim; raise your voice, fear not; say to the cities of Yehudah, "Behold your Elokim!"
Behold Havayah Elokim shall come with a strong hand, and His arm rules for Him; behold His reward is with Him, and His recompense is before Him.
Like a shepherd who tends his flock, with his arm he gathers lambs, and in his bosom he carries them, the nursing ones he leads.
Who measured water with his gait, and measured the heavens with his span, and measured by thirds the dust of the earth, and weighed mountains with a scale and hills with a balance?
Who meted the spirit of Havayah, and His adviser who informs Him?
With whom did He take counsel give him to understand, and teach him in the way of justice, and teach him knowledge, and the way of understandings did He let him know?
Behold the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and like dust on a balance are they counted; behold the islands are like fine dust that blows away.
And the Levanon — there is not enough to burn, and its beasts — there is not enough for burnt offerings.
All the nations are as nought before Him; as things of nought and vanity are they regarded by Him.
And to whom do you compare Elokim, and what likeness do you arrange for Him?
The graven image, the craftsman has melted, and the smith plates it with gold, and chains of silver he attaches.
He who is accustomed to select, chooses a tree that does not rot; he seeks for himself a skilled craftsman, to prepare a graven image, which will not move.
Do you not know, have you not heard has it not been told to you from the beginning? Do you not understand the foundations of the earth?
It is He Who sits above the circle of the earth, and whose inhabitants are like grasshoppers, who stretches out the heaven like a curtain, and He spread them out like a tent to dwell.
Who brings princes to nought, judges of the land He made like a thing of nought.

Even as though they were not planted, even as though they were not sown, even as though their trunk was not rooted in the earth; and also He blew on them, and they dried up, and a tempest shall carry them away like straw.
"Now, to whom will you compare Me that I should be equal?" the Holy One says.

Lift up your eyes on high and see, who created these, who takes out their host by number; all of them He calls by name; because of His great might and because He is strong in power, no one is missing.
Why should you say, O Yackov, and speak, O Yisroel, "My way has been hidden from Havayah, and from my Elokim, my judgment passes"?
Do you not know — if you have not heard — an everlasting Elokim is Havayah, the Creator of the ends of the earth; He neither tires nor wearies; there is no fathoming His understanding.
Who gives the tired strength, and to him who has no strength, He increases strength.
Now youths shall become tired and weary, and young men shall stumble.
But those who put their hope in Havayah shall renew their vigor, they shall raise wings as eagles; they shall run and not weary, they shall walk and not tire.
Be silent to Me, you islands, and kingdoms shall renew their strength; they shall approach, then they shall speak, together to judgment let us draw near.
Who aroused from the East, the one whom righteousness accompanied? He placed nations before him and over kings He gave him dominion; He made his sword like dust, his bow like wind-blown stubble.
He pursued them and passed on safely, on a path upon which he had not come with his feet.
Who worked and did, Who calls the generations from the beginning; I, Havayah, am first, and with the last ones I am He.
The islands shall see and fear; the ends of the earth shall quake; they have approached and come.
Each one shall aid his fellow, and to his brother he shall say, "Strengthen yourself."

And the craftsman strengthened the smith, the one who smooths with the hammer strengthened the one who wields the sledge hammer; he says of the cement, "It is good," and he strengthened it with nails that it should not move.
But you, Yisroel My servant, Yackov whom I have chosen, the seed of Avraham, who loved Me,
Whom I grasped from the ends of the earth, and from its nobles I called you, and I said to you, "You are My servant"; I chose you and I did not despise you.
Do not fear for I am with you; be not discouraged for I am your Elokim: I encouraged you, I also helped you, I also supported you with My righteous hand.
Behold all those incensed against you shall be ashamed and confounded; those who quarreled with you shall be as nought and be lost.
You may seek them but not find them, those who quarrel with you; those who war with you shall be as nought and as nothing.
For I, Havayah your Elokim, grasp your right hand; Who says to you, "Fear not, I help you."
Fear not, O worm of Yackov, the number of Yisroel; "I have helped you," Havayah says, and your redeemer, the Holy One of Yisroel.
Behold I have made you a new grooved threshing-sledge, with sharp points; you shall thresh the mountains and crush them fine, and you shall make hills like chaff.
You shall winnow them, and a wind shall carry them off, and a tempest shall scatter them, and you shall rejoice with Havayah, with the Holy One of Yisroel shall you praise yourself.
The poor and the needy seek water, but there is none; their tongue is parched with thirst; I, Havayah, will answer them, I, the Elokim of Yisroel, will not forsake them.
I will open rivers on the high places, and springs in the midst of valleys; I will make a desert into a pool of water and a wasteland into sources of water.
I will give in the desert cedars, acacia trees, myrtles, and pines; I will place in the wilderness boxtrees, firs, and cypresses together.
In order that they see and know, and pay attention and understand together that the hand of Havayah did this and the Holy One of Yisroel created it.
"Present your plea," Havayah says; "present your strong points," says the King of Yackov.
Let them present and tell us what will happen; the first things what were they? Tell, and we will take it to heart, and we will know their end, or the coming events let us hear.
Tell the signs coming later, and we will know, for you are gods; you will even benefit and harm; let us talk and let us see together.
Behold you are of nought, and your deed is one of shouting; the abominable one will select you.
I have aroused from the north and he came; from the rising of the sun he shall call in My name. And he shall come upon princes like mortar and as the potter treads clay.
Who told from the beginning that we may know, and from before, that we may say, "He is just"? Not one told; not one let us hear; not one hears your statements.
The first one to Tziyon, behold, behold them, and for Yerushalayim I will give a herald.
And I look, and there is no man, and of these, and there is no counselor, and I ask them that they reply with a word.
Behold them all, their deeds are nought, of no substance; wind and nothingness are their molten images.
Behold My servant, I will support him, My chosen one, whom My soul desires; I have placed My spirit upon him, he shall promulgate justice to the nations.
He shall neither cry nor shall he raise his voice; and he shall not make his voice heard outside.
A breaking reed he shall not break; and a flickering flaxen wick he shall not quench; with truth shall he execute justice.
Neither shall he weaken nor shall he be broken, until he establishes justice in the land, and for his instruction, islands shall long.

So Elokim Havayah said, the Creator of the heavens and the One Who stretched them out, Who spread out the earth and what springs forth from it, Who gave a soul to the people upon it and a spirit to those who walk thereon.
I am Havayah; I called you with righteousness and I will strengthen your hand; and I formed you, and I made you for a people's covenant, for a light to nations.
To open blind eyes, to bring prisoners out of a dungeon, those who sit in darkness out of a prison.
I am Havayah, that is My Name; and My glory I will not give to another, nor My praise to the graven images.
The former things, behold they have come to pass, and the new things I tell; before they sprout I will let you hear.
Sing to Havayah a new song, His praise from the end of the earth, those who go down to the sea and those therein, the islands and their inhabitants.
The desert and its cities shall raise their voice; Keidar shall be inhabited with villages; the rock dwellers shall exult, from the mountain peaks they shall shout.
They shall give glory to Havayah, and they shall recite His praise on the islands.
The Havayah shall go out like a hero; like a warrior shall He arouse zeal; He shall shout, He shall even cry, He shall overpower His foes.
I was silent from time immemorial; I am still, I restrain Myself. Like a travailing woman will I cry; I will be terrified and destroy them together.
I will destroy mountains and hills, and all their grass I will dry out, and I will make rivers into islands and I will dry up the pools.

And I will lead the blind on a road they did not know; in paths they did not know I will lead them; I will make darkness into light before them, and crooked paths into straight ones. These things, I will do them and I will not forsake them.
They shall turn back greatly ashamed, those who trust in the graven image, who say to the molten idols, "You are our gods."
You deaf ones, listen, and you blind ones, look to see.
Who is blind but My servant, and deaf as My messenger whom I will send? He who was blind is as the one who received his payment, and he who was blind is as the servant of Havayah.
There is much to see but you do not observe, to open the ears but no one listens.
The Havayah desires this for His righteousness' sake; He magnifies the Torah and strengthens it.
And it is a robbed and pillaged people; all their youths are grieved, and they are hidden in dungeons; they are subject to plunderers, and none rescues them, to pillagers, and no one says, "Return."
Who among you will hearken to this, will listen and hear for the future?
Who subjected Yackov to plunder and Yisroel to spoilers? Was it not Havayah? This, that we sinned against Him, and they did not want to go in His way and did not hearken to His Torah.
And He poured out upon them the fury of His anger and the strength of battle, and it blazed upon them all around and they did not know, and it burned among them and they did not take heed.
And now, so Havayah said, your Creator, O Yackov, and the One Who formed you, O Yisroel, "Do not fear, for I have redeemed you, and I called by your name, you are Mine.
When you pass through water, I am with you, and in rivers, they shall not overflow you; when you go amidst fire, you shall not be burnt, neither shall a flame burn amongst you.
For I am Havayah your Elokim, the Holy One of Yisroel, your Savior; I have given Mitzrayim as your ransom, Kush and Seva in your stead.
Since you are dear in My eyes, you were honored and I loved you, and I give men in your stead and nations instead of your life.
Fear not for I am with you; from the east I will bring your seed, and from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north, "Give," and to the south, "Do not refrain"; bring My sons from afar and My daughters from the end of the earth."
Everyone that is called by My name, and whom I created for My glory, I formed him, yea I made him.
To bring out a blind people, who have eyes, and deaf ones who have ears.

Were all the nations gathered together, and kingdoms assembled, who of them would tell this or let us know of the first events? Let them present their witnesses, and they shall be deemed just, and let them hear and say, "True."
"You are My witnesses," Havayah says, "and My servant whom I chose," in order that you know and believe Me, and understand that I am He; before Me no deity was formed and after Me none shall be.
I, I am Havayah, and besides Me there is no savior.
I told and I saved, and I made heard and there was no stranger among you, and you are My witnesses," Havayah says, "and I am Elokim.
Even before the day I am He, and there is no saving from My hand; I do, and who retracts it?"
So Havayah said, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Yisroel, "Because of you, I sent you to Bavel, and I lowered, them all with oars, and Kasdim in the ships of their rejoicing.
I am Havayah, your Holy One, the Creator of Yisroel, your King.
So Havayah said, who made a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters.
Who drew out chariots and horses, army and power; they lay together, they did not rise; they were extinguished, like a flaxen wick they were quenched.
Remember not the first events, and do not meditate over early ones.
Behold I am making a new thing, now it will sprout, now you shall know it; yea I will make a road in the desert, rivers in the wasteland.
The beasts of the field shall honor Me, the jackals and the ostriches, for I gave water in the desert, rivers in the wasteland, to give My chosen people drink.
This people I formed for Myself; they shall recite My praise.
But you did not call Me, O Yackov, for you wearied of Me, O Yisroel.
You did not bring Me the lambs of your burnt offerings, nor did you honor Me with your sacrifices; neither did I overwork you with meal-offerings nor did I weary you with frankincense.
Neither did you purchase cane for Me with money, nor have you sated Me with the fat of your sacrifices. But you have burdened Me with your sins; you have wearied Me with your iniquities.
I, yea I erase your transgressions for My sake, and your sins I will not remember.
Remind Me, let us stand in judgment; you tell, in order that you be accounted just.
Your first father sinned, and your intercessors transgressed against Me.
And I profane the holy princes, and I deliver Yackov to destruction and Yisroel to revilings.
And now, hearken, Yackov My servant, and Yisroel whom I have chosen.
So Havayah said your Maker, and He Who formed you from the womb shall aid you. Fear not, My servant Yackov, and Yeshurun whom I have chosen.
As I will pour water on the thirsty and running water on dry land, I will pour My spirit on your seed and My blessing on your offspring.
And they shall sprout among the grass like willows on rivulets of water.
This one shall say, "I am Havayah's," and this one shall call himself by the name of Yackov, and this one shall write with his hand, "To Havayah," and adopt the name Yisroel.
So Havayah said, the King of Yisroel and his Redeemer Havayah of Hosts, "I am first and I am last, and besides Me there is no deity.
And who will call that he is like Me and will tell it and arrange it for Me, since My placing the ancient people, and the signs and those that will come, let them tell for themselves.
Fear not and be not dismayed; did I not let you hear it from then, and I told it and you are My witnesses; is there a deity besides Me? And there is no rock I did not know.
Those who form idols are all of them vanity, and their treasures are of no avail, and they are their witnesses; they neither see nor hear, nor do they know, so that they be ashamed.
Who formed a deity or molded an image, being of no avail?
Behold, all his colleagues shall be ashamed, and they are smiths — of man. Let all of them gather, let them stand, they shall fear, they shall be ashamed together.

The ironsmith makes an axe, and he works with coal, and with sledge hammers he fashions it; and he made it with his strong arm; yea he is hungry, and he has no strength, he did not drink water and he becomes faint.

The carpenter stretched out a line, he beautifies it with a saw; he fixes it with planes, and with a compass he rounds it, and he made it in the likeness of a man, like the beauty of man to sit in the house.
To hew for himself cedars, and he took an ilex and an oak and he reenforced it with forest trees; he planted a sapling, and rain makes it grow.
And it was for man to ignite, and he took from them and warmed himself; he even heated the oven and baked bread; he even made a deity and prostrated himself, he made a graven image and bowed to them.
Half of it he burnt with fire, on half of it he ate meat, he roasted a roast and became sated; he even warmed himself and said, "Aha, I am warm, I see fire."
And what is left over from it he made for a deity, for his graven image; he kneels to it and prostrates himself and prays to it, and he says, "Save me, for you are my deity."
Neither do they know nor do they understand, for their eyes are bedaubed from seeing, their hearts from understanding.

And he does not give it thought, and he has neither knowledge nor understanding to say, "Half of it I burnt with fire, and I even baked bread on its coals, I roasted meat and ate. And what was left over from it, shall I make for an abomination, shall I bow to rotten wood?"
To a provider made of ashes, a deceived heart has perverted him, and he shall not save his soul, and he shall not say, "Is there not falsehood in my right hand?"
Remember these, O Yackov; and Yisroel, for you are My servant; I formed you that you be a servant to Me, Yisroel, do not forget Me.
I erased your transgressions like a thick cloud, and like a cloud have I erased your sins; return to Me for I have redeemed you.

Sing, ye heavens, for Havayah has done this, shout, ye lowest parts of the earth; ye mountains, burst out in song, the forest and all trees therein; for Havayah has redeemed Yackov, and with Yisroel shall He be glorified.
So Havayah said, your Redeemer, and the One Who formed you from the womb, "I am Havayah Who makes everything, Who stretched forth the heavens alone, Who spread out the earth from My power.
Who frustrates the signs of imposters, and diviners He makes mad; He turns the wise backwards, and makes their knowledge foolish.

He fulfills the word of His servant, and the counsel of His messenger He completes; Who says of Yerushalayim, "It shall be settled," and of the cities of Yehudah, "They shall be built, and its ruins I will erect."
Who says to the deep, "Be dry, and I will dry up your rivers."
Who says of Koresh, "He is My shepherd, and all My desire he shall fulfill," and to say of Yerushalayim, "It shall be built, and the Temple shall be founded."

So Havayah said to His anointed one, to Koresh, whose right hand I held, to flatten nations before him, and the loins of kings I will loosen, to open portals before him, and gates shall not be closed.
I will go before you, and I will straighten out crooked paths; I will break portals of copper and cut off bars of iron.
And I will give you treasures of darkness, and riches hidden in secret places, in order that you know that I am Havayah Who calls you by your name — the Holy One of Yisroel.
For the sake of My servant Yackov, and Yisroel My chosen one, and I called out to you by your name; I surnamed you, yet you have not known Me.
I am Havayah, and there is no other; besides Me there is no Elokim: I will strengthen you although you have not known Me.
In order that they know from the shining of the sun and from the west that there is no one besides Me; I am Havayah and there is no other.
Who forms light and creates darkness, Who makes peace and creates evil; I am Havayah, Who makes all these.

Cause the heavens above to drip, and let the skies pour down righteousness; let the earth open, and let salvation and righteousness be fruitful; let it cause them to sprout together; I, Havayah, have created it.
Woe to him who contends with his Creator, a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth, shall the clay say to its potter, "What do you make? And your work has no place."
Woe to him who says to a father, "What do you beget?" and to a woman, "Why do you experience birth pangs?"
So Havayah said, the Holy One of Yisroel, and his Creator, "Ask Me about the signs; concerning My children and the work of My hands do you command Me?
I made the earth, and I created man upon it; as for Me — My hands stretched out the heavens, and I ordained their host.
I aroused him with righteousness, and all his ways I will straighten out. He shall build My city and free My exiles, neither for a price nor for a bribe," Havayah of Hosts said.

So Havayah said, "The toil of Mitzrayim and the merchandise of Kush and the Shevaim, men of stature, shall come over to you and shall be yours; they shall follow you; they shall come over in chains, and they shall prostrate themselves before you, they shall pray to you, "Only in you is Elokim and there is no other deity.
Indeed, You are a Elokim Who conceals Himself, the Elokim of Yisroel, the Savior.
They shall be ashamed, yea disgraced, all of them the master painters shall go together in disgrace.
Yisroel shall be saved by Havayah with an everlasting salvation; you shall neither be ashamed nor disgraced to all eternity.

For so Havayah said, the Creator of heaven, Who is Elokim, Who formed the earth and made it, He established it; He did not create it for a waste, He formed it to be inhabited, "I am Havayah and there is no other.
Not in secret did I speak, in a place of a land of darkness; I did not say to the seed of Yackov, Seek Me, in vain; I am Havayah, Who speaks righteousness, declares things that are right.
Assemble and come, approach together, you survivors of the nations; those who carry their graven wooden image and pray to a deity who does not save, do not know.

Declare and present, let them even take counsel together; who announced this from before, who declared it from then? Is it not I, Havayah, and there are no other gods besides Me, a just and saving Elokim there is not besides Me.
Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am Elokim, and there is no other.
By Myself I swore, righteousness emanated from My mouth, a word, and it shall not be retracted, that to Me shall every knee kneel, every tongue shall swear."
But to me did He say by Havayah righteousness and strength, to Him shall come and be ashamed all who are incensed against Him.
Through Havayah shall all the seed of Yisroel find righteousness and boast.
Bel squats; Nevo soils himself; their idols were to the beasts and to the cattle; what you carry is made a load, a burden for the weary.
They soiled themselves, yea they squatted together, they could not deliver the burden, and they themselves have gone into captivity.
Hearken to Me, the house of Yackov, and all the remnant of the house of Yisroel, who are borne from birth, carried from the womb.
And until old age I am the same, and until you turn gray I will carry; I have made and I will bear and I will carry and deliver.
To whom shall you liken Me and make Me equal and compare Me that we may be alike?
Those who let gold run from the purse and weigh silver with the balance; they hire a goldsmith and he makes it a deity, they kneel, yea they prostrate themselves.

They bear it, on the shoulder they carry it, and they put it in its place and it stands, from its place it does not move; yea he cries to it and it does not answer; from his distress it does not save him.
Remember this and strengthen yourselves, take to heart, you transgressors.
Remember the first things of old, that I am Elokim and there is no other; I am Elokim and there is none like Me.
I tell the end from the beginning, and from before, what was not done; I say, 'My counsel shall stand, and all My desire I will do.'
I call from the east a swift bird, from a distant land the man of My counsel; yea I spoke, I will also bring it; I formed it, I will also do it.
Hearken to Me, you stout-hearted, that are far from righteousness.
I have brought near My righteousness, it shall not go far, and My salvation shall not delay, and I will give salvation in Tziyon, to Yisroel, My glory.
Descend and sit on the dust, virgin daughter of Bavel, sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Kasdim, for no longer shall they call you tender and delicate.
Take millstones and grind flour, bare your covered parts, uncover the paths, bare your leg, cross rivers.
Your nakedness shall be uncovered; yea your shame shall be seen; I will take revenge and I will not entreat any man.
Our redeemer, Havayah of Hosts is His name, the Holy One of Yisroel.
Sit silently and come into the darkness, O daughter of the Kasdim, for they shall no longer call you mistress of kingdoms.
I became wroth with My people, I violated My heritage, and I delivered them into your hand; you did not show them mercy; on the aged you made your yoke very heavy.
And you said, "I will forever be a mistress," until you did not take these to heart, you did not remember its end.
And now, hearken to this, delicate one, who sits securely, who says to herself, "I am it, and there is none besides me; I will not sit as a widow; neither will I know bereavement."

And these two shall come to you in a second in one day, bereavement and widowhood; in their full measure, they shall come upon you with the multitude of your sorceries, with the great abundance of your charms.
And you trusted in your evil, you said, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and your knowledge — that perverted you. And you said to yourself, "I am it, and there is none besides me."

And evil shall come upon you, you shall not know how to remove it by prayer; and calamity shall befall you, you shall not know how to rid yourself of it; and desolation shall come upon you suddenly, you shall not know.
Stand now with your charms and with the multitude of your sorceries, in which you toiled since your youth; perhaps you will be able to help, perhaps you will gain strength.
You have wearied with the multitude of your counsels; let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators of what will come upon you, stand up and save you.
Behold they were like stubble, fire burnt them, they shall not save themselves from the power of the flame; there is no coal by which to warm oneself, or fire opposite which to sit.
So were they to you, those for whom you toiled; your traffickers since your youth, each one strayed to his side, no one saves you.

Hearken to this, O house of Yackov, who are called by the name of Yisroel, and who emanated from the waters of Yehudah, who swear by the name of Havayah and make mention of the Elokim of Yisroel, neither in truth nor in righteousness.
For they are called as being from the Holy City, and they leaned on the Elokim of Yisroel; Havayah of Hosts is His name.
The first things I told from then, and they emanated from My mouth and I let you hear them; suddenly I did them and they came to pass.
Because of My knowledge that you are obstinate, and your nape is a sinew of iron, and your forehead is brazen.
And I told you from then; when it had not yet come to pass I let you hear it; lest you say, "My idol performed them, and my graven image and my molten image ordained them."
You have heard, see all of it; and you, will you not tell? I let you hear new things from now, and hidden things that you did not know.
Now they have been created and not from then, and before the day, and you did not hear them, lest you say, "I knew them."
Neither did you hearken, neither did you know, nor was your ear opened from then, for I knew that you would deal treacherously, and you were called transgressor from the womb.
For the sake of My name I defer My anger, and My praise is that I restrain My wrath for you, not to cut you off.
Behold I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen for you the crucible of poverty.
For My sake, for My sake I will do, for how shall it be profaned? And My honor I will not give to another.
Hearken to Me, O Yackov, and Yisroel, who was called by Me, I am He, I am first, yea I am last.
Even My hand laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand measured the heavens with handbreadths; I call them, they stand together.
All of you, gather and hearken, who of them told these? The Havayah loves him, who shall do His work in Bavel and show His arm upon the Kasdim.
I, yea I spoke, I even called him, I brought him, and his way prospered.
Draw near to Me, hearken to this; in the beginning I did not speak in secret, from the time it was, there was I, and now, Havayah Elokim has sent me, and His spirit.
So Havayah said, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Yisroel, "I am Havayah your Elokim, Who teaches you for your profit, Who leads you by the way you should go.
Had you hearkened to My commandments, your peace would be as a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
And your seed would be like the sand and those emanating from your innards would be like its innards; his name shall neither be cut off nor destroyed from before Me.
Leave Bavel, flee from the Kasdim; with a voice of singing declare, tell this, publicize it to the end of the earth; say, "The Havayah has redeemed His servant Yackov."
And they did not thirst when He led them in the wastelands, He made water run from a rock for them; He split a rock and water flowed.
"There is no peace," Havayah said. "for the wicked."
Hearken, you islands, to me, and listen closely, you nations, from afar; Havayah called me from the womb, from the innards of my mother He mentioned my name.
And He made my mouth like a sharp sword, He concealed me in the shadow of His hand; and He made me into a polished arrow, He hid me in His quiver.
And He said to me, "You are My servant, Yisroel, about whom I will boast."
And I said, "I toiled in vain, I consumed my strength for nought and vanity." Yet surely my right is with Havayah, and my deed is with my Elokim.

And now, Havayah, Who formed me from the womb as a servant to Him, said to bring Yackov back to Him, and Yisroel shall be gathered to Him, and I will be honored in the eyes of Havayah, and my Elokim was my strength.

And He said, "It is too light for you to be My servant, to establish the tribes of Yackov and to bring back the besieged of Yisroel, but I will make you a light of nations, so that My salvation shall be until the end of the earth."

So Havayah said, the Redeemer of Yisroel, his Holy One, about him who is despised of men, about him whom the nation abhors, about a slave of rulers, "Kings shall see and rise, princes, and they shall prostrate themselves, for the sake of Havayah Who is faithful, the Holy One of Yisroel, and He chose you."

So Havayah said, "In a time of favor I answered you, and on a day of salvation I helped you; and I will watch you, and I will make you for a people of a covenant, to establish a land, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages.
To say to the prisoners, "Go out!" and to the darkness, "Show yourselves!" By the roads they shall graze, and by all rivers is their pasture.
They shall neither hunger nor thirst, nor shall the heat and the sun smite them, for He Who has mercy on them shall lead them, and by the springs of water He shall guide them.
And I will make all My mountains into a road, and My highways shall be raised.
Behold, these shall come from afar, and behold these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.
Sing, O heavens, and rejoice, O earth, and mountains burst out in song, for Havayah has consoled His people, and He shall have mercy on His poor.
And Tziyon said, "The Havayah has forsaken me, and Havayah has forgotten me."
Shall a woman forget her sucking child, from having mercy on the child of her womb? These too shall forget, but I will not forget you.
Behold on My hands have I engraved you; your walls are before Me always.
Your sons have hastened; those who destroy you and those who lay you waste shall go forth from you.
Lift your eyes around and see, all of them have gathered, have come to you; as I live, Havayah says, that you shall wear all of them as jewelry, and you shall tie them as a bride.
For your ruins and your desolate places and your land that has been destroyed, for now you shall be crowded by the inhabitants, and those who would destroy you shall be far away.
Your children of whom you were bereaved shall yet say in your ears, "The place is too narrow for me; move over for me so that I will dwell."
And you shall say to yourself, "Who begot these for me, seeing that I am bereaved and solitary, exiled and rejected, and who raised these? Behold I was left alone; these — from where are they?"

So Havayah Elokim said, "Behold I will raise My hand to the nations, and to the peoples will I raise My standard, and they shall bring your sons in their armpits, and your daughters shall be borne on their shoulders.

And kings shall be your nursing fathers and their princesses your wet nurses; they shall prostrate themselves to you with their face on the ground, and they shall lick the dust of your feet, and you shall know that I am Havayah, for those who wait for Me shall not be ashamed.
Shall prey be taken from a mighty warrior, or shall the captives of the righteous escape?"
For so Havayah said, "Even the captives of a mighty warrior can be taken and the prey of a tyrant shall escape, and with your contender will I contend, and your sons I will save.

And those who taunt you — I will feed their flesh, and as with sweet wine they shall become drunk from their blood; and all flesh shall know that I am Havayah Who saves you, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Yackov.

So Havayah said, "Where is your mother's bill of divorce that I sent her away? Or, who is it of My creditors to whom I sold you? Behold for your iniquities you were sold, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.

Why have I come and there is no man? Why have I called and no one answers? Is My hand too short to redeem, or do I have no strength to save? Behold, with My rebuke I dry up the sea, I make rivers into a desert; their fish become foul because there is no water and die because of thirst.
I clothe the heavens with darkness, and I make sackcloth their raiment.
The Havayah Elokim gave me a tongue for teaching, to know to establish times for the faint for His word; He awakens me every morning, He awakens My ear, to hear according to the teachings.
The Havayah Elokim opened my ear, and I did not rebel; I did not turn away backwards.
I gave my back to smiters and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair; I did not hide my face from embarrassments and spitting.
But Havayah Elokim helps me, therefore, I was not embarrassed; therefore, I made my face like flint, and I knew that I would not be ashamed.
He Who vindicates me is near, whoever wishes to quarrel with me — let us stand together; whoever is my contender shall approach me.
Behold, Havayah Elokim shall help me; who is he that will condemn me? Behold all of them shall wear out like a garment, a moth shall consume them.
Who among you is Elokim — fearing, who hearkens to the voice of His servant, who went in darkness and who has no light, let him trust in the name of Havayah and lean on his Elokim.
Behold all of you who kindle fire, who give power to flames; go in the flame of your fire, and in the flames you have kindled; from My hand has this come to you, in grief you shall lie down.
Hearken to Me, you pursuers of righteousness, you seekers of Havayah; look at the rock whence you were hewn and at the hole of the pit whence you were dug.
Look at Avraham your father and at Sarah who bore you, for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him and made him many.

For Havayah shall console Tziyon, He shall console all its ruins, and He shall make its desert like a paradise and its wasteland like the garden of Havayah; joy and happiness shall be found therein, thanksgiving and a voice of song.
Hearken to Me, My people, and My nation, bend your ears to Me, when Torah shall emanate from Me, and My judgment shall be for the light of the peoples, I will give them rest.
My righteousness is near, My salvation has gone forth, and My arms shall chasten peoples; islands shall wait for Me, and on My arm shall they trust.

Raise your eyes to heaven and look at the earth from beneath, for the heavens shall vanish like smoke, and the earth shall rot away like a garment, and its inhabitants shall likewise die, and My salvation shall be forever, and My righteousness shall not be abolished.
Hearken to Me, you who know righteousness, a people that has My Torah in their heart, fear not reproach of man, and from their revilings be not dismayed.
For, like a garment, the moth shall consume them, and like wool, the worm shall consume them, but My righteousness shall be forever, and My salvation to all generations.
Awaken, awaken, dress yourself with strength, O arm of Havayah, awaken, awaken like days of old, generations of yore; are you not the one that hewed Rahav and slew the sea monster?
Are you not the one who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep? Who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed ones to pass?
And the redeemed of Havayah shall return, and they shall come to Tziyon with song, and with everlasting joy on their heads; gladness and joy shall overtake them; sorrow and sighing shall flee.
I, yea I am He Who consoles you; who are you that you fear man who will die and the son of man, who shall be made as grass?

And you forgot Havayah your Maker, Who spread out the heavens and founded the earth, and you fear constantly the whole day because of the wrath of the oppressor when he prepared to destroy. Now where is the wrath of the oppressor?
What must be poured out hastened to be opened, and he shall not die of destruction, and his bread shall not be wanting.
I am Havayah your Elokim, Who wrinkles the sea and its waves stir; Havayah of Hosts is His name.
And I placed My words into your mouth, and with the shadow of My hand I covered you, to plant the heavens and to found the earth and to say to Tziyon that you are My people.
Awaken, awaken, arise, Yerushalayim, for you have drunk from the hand of Havayah the cup of His wrath; the dregs of the cup of weakness you have drained.
She has no guide out of all the sons she bore, and she has no one who takes her by the hand out of all the sons she raised.
These two things have befallen you; who will lament for you? Plunder and destruction, and famine and sword. With whom will I console you?
Your sons have fainted, they lie at the entrance of all streets like a wild ox in a net, full of the wrath of Havayah, the rebuke of your Elokim.
Therefore, hearken now to this, you poor one, and who is drunk but not from wine.
So said your Master, Havayah, and your Elokim Who shall judge His people, "Behold, I took from you the cup of weakness; the dregs of the cup of My wrath — you shall no longer continue to drink it.

And I will place it into the hand of those who cause you to wander, who said to your soul, 'Bend down and let us cross,' and you made your body like the earth and like the street for those who cross."
Awaken, awaken, put on your strength, O Tziyon; put on the garments of your beauty, Yerushalayim the Holy City, for no longer shall the uncircumcised or the unclean continue to enter you.
Shake yourselves from the dust, arise, sit down, O Yerushalayim; free yourself of the bands of your neck, O captive daughter of Tziyon.
For so Havayah said, "You were sold for nought, and you shall not be redeemed for money."
For so Havayah Elokim said, "My people first went down to Mitzrayim to sojourn there, but Ashur oppressed them for nothing."
"And now, what have I here," Havayah says, "that My people has been taken for nothing. His rulers boast," Havayah says, "and constantly all day My name is blasphemed.
Therefore, My people shall know My name; therefore, on that day, for I am He Who speaks, here I am."
How beautiful are the feet of the herald on the mountains, announcing peace, heralding good tidings, announcing salvation, saying to Tziyon, "Your Elokim has manifested His kingdom."
The voice of your watchmen — they raised a voice, together they shall sing, for eye to eye they shall see when Havayah returns to Tziyon.
Burst out in song, sing together, O ruins of Yerushalayim, for Havayah has consoled His people; He has redeemed Yerushalayim.
The Havayah has revealed His holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our Elokim.
Turn away, turn away, get out of there, touch no unclean one; get out of its midst, purify yourselves, you who bear Havayah's vessels.
For not with haste shall you go forth and not in a flurry of flight shall you go, for Havayah goes before you, and your rear guard is the Elokim of Yisroel.
Behold My servant shall prosper; he shall be exalted and lifted up, and he shall be very high.
As many wondered about you, "How marred his appearance is from that of a man, and his features from that of people!"
So shall he cast down many nations; kings shall shut their mouths because of him, for, what had not been told them they saw, and at what they had not heard they gazed.
Who would have believed our report, and to whom was the arm of Havayah revealed?
And he came up like a sapling before it, and like a root from dry ground, he had neither form nor comeliness; and we saw him that he had no appearance. Now shall we desire him?
Despised and rejected by men, a man of pains and accustomed to illness, and as one who hides his face from us, despised and we held him of no account.
Indeed, he bore our illnesses, and our pains — he carried them, yet we accounted him as plagued, smitten by Elokim and oppressed.
But he was pained because of our transgressions, crushed because of our iniquities; the chastisement of our welfare was upon him, and with his wound we were healed.
We all went astray like sheep, we have turned, each one on his way, and Havayah accepted his prayers for the iniquity of all of us.

He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he would not open his mouth; like a lamb to the slaughter he would be brought, and like a ewe that is mute before her shearers, and he would not open his mouth.
From imprisonment and from judgment he is taken, and his generation who shall tell? For he was cut off from the land of the living; because of the transgression of my people, a plague befell them.
And he gave his grave to the wicked, and to the wealthy with his kinds of death, because he committed no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.
And Havayah wished to crush him, He made him ill; if his soul makes itself restitution, he shall see children, he shall prolong his days, and Elokim's purpose shall prosper in his hand.
From the toil of his soul he would see, he would be satisfied; with his knowledge My servant would vindicate the just for many, and their iniquities he would bear.

Therefore, I will allot him a portion in public, and with the strong he shall share plunder, because he poured out his soul to death, and with transgressors he was counted; and he bore the sin of many, and interceded for the transgressors.

"Sing you barren woman who has not borne; burst out into song and jubilate, you who have not experienced birth pangs, for the children of the desolate one are more than the children of the married woman," Havayah says.
Widen the place of your tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of your habitations, do not spare; lengthen your cords and strengthen your stakes.
For right and left shall you prevail, and your seed shall inherit nations and repeople desolate cities.

Fear not, for you shall not be ashamed, and be not embarrassed for you shall not be put to shame, for the shame of your youth you shall forget, and the disgrace of your widowhood you shall no longer remember.
For your Master is your Maker, Havayah of Hosts is His name, and your Redeemer, the Holy One of Yisroel, shall be called the Elokim of all the earth.
For, like a wife who is deserted and distressed in spirit has Havayah called you, and a wife of one's youth who was rejected, said your Elokim.
"For a small moment have I forsaken you, and with great mercy will I gather you.
With a little wrath did I hide My countenance for a moment from you, and with everlasting kindness will I have compassion on you," said your Redeemer, Havayah.
"For this is to Me as the waters of Noach, as I swore that the waters of Noach shall never again pass over the earth, so have I sworn neither to be wroth with you nor to rebuke you.
For the mountains shall depart and the hills totter, but My kindness shall not depart from you, neither shall the covenant of My peace totter," Havayah says, Who has compassion on you.
O poor tempestuous one, who was not consoled, behold I will set your stones with carbuncle, and I will lay your foundations with sapphires.
And I will make your windows of jasper and your gates of carbuncle stones, and all your border of precious stones.
And all your children shall be disciples of Havayah, and your children's peace shall increase.
With righteousness shall you be established, go far away from oppression, for you shall not fear, and from ruin, for it will not come near you.
Behold, the one with whom I am not, shall fear, whoever mobilizes against you shall defect to you.
Behold I have created a smith, who blows on a charcoal fire and produces a weapon for his work, and I have created a destroyer to destroy it.

Any weapon whetted against you shall not succeed, and any tongue that contends with you in judgment, you shall condemn; this is the heritage of the servants of Havayah and their due reward from Me, Havayah says.
Ho! All who thirst, go to water, and whoever has no money, go, buy and eat, and go, buy without money and without a price, wine and milk.
Why should you weigh out money without bread and your toil without satiety? Hearken to Me and eat what is good, and your soul shall delight in fatness.
Incline your ear and come to Me, hearken and your soul shall live, and I will make for you an everlasting covenant, the dependable mercies of Dovid.
Behold, a witness to nations have I appointed him, a ruler and a commander of nations.
Behold, a nation you do not know you shall call, and a nation that did not know you shall run to you, for the sake of Havayah your Elokim and for the Holy One of Yisroel, for He glorified you.
Seek Havayah when He is found, call Him when He is near.
The wicked shall give up his way, and the man of iniquity his thoughts, and he shall return to Havayah, Who shall have mercy upon him, and to our Elokim, for He will freely pardon.
"For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways," Havayah says.
"As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways and My thoughts higher than your thoughts.

For, just as the rain and the snow fall from the heavens, and it does not return there, unless it has satiated the earth and fructified it and furthered its growth, and has given seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
so shall be My word that emanates from My mouth; it shall not return to Me empty, unless it has done what I desire and has made prosperous the one to whom I sent it.
For with joy shall you go forth, and with peace shall you be brought; the mountains and the hills shall burst into song before you, and all the trees of the field shall clap hands.
Instead of the briar, a cypress shall rise, and instead of the nettle, a myrtle shall rise, and it shall be for Havayah as a name, as an everlasting sign, which shall not be discontinued."
So Havayah says, "Keep justice and practice righteousness, for My salvation is near to come, and My benevolence to be revealed."
Fortunate is the man who will do this and the person who will hold fast to it, he who keeps the Shabbos from profaning it and guards his hand from doing any evil.
Now let not the foreigner who joined Havayah, say, "The Havayah will surely separate me from His people," and let not the eunuch say, "Behold, I am a dry tree."
For so Havayah says to the eunuchs who will keep My Shabbosos and will choose what I desire and hold fast to My covenant,
"I will give them in My house and in My walls a place and a name, better than sons and daughters; an everlasting name I will give him, which will not be discontinued.
And the foreigners who join with Havayah to serve Him and to love the name of Havayah, to be His servants, everyone who observes the Shabbos from profaning it and who holds fast to My covenant.

I will bring them to My holy mount, and I will cause them to rejoice in My house of prayer, their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be acceptable upon My altar, for My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
So Havayah Elokim says, Who gathers in the dispersed of Yisroel, I will yet gather others to him, together with his gathered ones.
All the beasts of the field, come to devour all the beasts in the forest.
His lookouts are all blind, they do not know, dumb dogs who cannot bark; they lie slumbering, loving to slumber.
And the dogs are of greedy disposition, they know not satiety; and they are shepherds who know not to understand; they all turned to their way, each one to his gain, every last one.
"Come, I will take wine, and let us guzzle old wine, and tomorrow shall be like this, but greater and much more."
The righteous man has perished, but no one takes it to heart, and men of kindness are taken away, with no one understanding that because of the evil the righteous man has been taken away.
He shall come in peace; they shall rest in their resting-place, whoever walks in his uprightness.
And you, draw near hither, children of sorcery; children who commit adultery, and played the whore.
On whom will you rely to enjoy yourselves; against whom do you open your mouth wide; against whom do you stick out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, seed of falsehood?
You who inflame yourselves among the terebinths, under every green tree, who slaughter the children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks.
Of the smooth stones of the valley is your portion; they, they are your lot; to them too you have poured out libations, offered up sacrifices; in the face of these shall I relent?
On a high and lofty mountain you placed your couch; there too you went to slaughter sacrifices.

And behind the door and the doorpost you have directed your thoughts, for while with Me, you uncovered us and went up, you widened your couch and made for yourself a covenant with them; you loved their couch, you chose a place.
And you brought a gift to the king with oil, and you increased your perfumes; and you sent your ambassadors far off, and you humbled them to the grave.
